nodes.name: Sárközy's theorem
nodes.statement: In the '70s, S\'{a}rk\"{o}zy{} \cite{sarkozy1978} proved that any subset of integers with positive upper density contains two elements differing by a perfect square.
assumptions: any subset of integers with positive upper density
conclusions: contains two elements differing by a perfect square
nodes.statement_short: Every set of integers of positive upper density contains two elements differing by a perfect square.

nodes.name: Sárközy's quantitative bound
nodes.statement: In fact, he proved that if a set does not contain two elements differing by a perfect square, then its density up to $N$ is ${\rm O}\bigl((\log\log N)^{2/3} (\log N)^{-1/3}\bigr)$.
assumptions: if a set does not contain two elements differing by a perfect square
conclusions: its density up to $N$ is ${\rm O}\bigl((\log\log N)^{2/3} (\log N)^{-1/3}\bigr)$
nodes.statement_short: A square-difference-free set has density $O((\log\log N)^{2/3}(\log N)^{-1/3})$ up to $N$.

nodes.name: Sárközy's theorem for intersective polynomials
nodes.statement: As it turns out, one can replace $P(x) = x^2$ in S\'{a}rk\"{o}zy{}'s theorem with any intersective polynomial, i.e., any polynomial that has a root modulo every prime.
assumptions: any intersective polynomial, i.e., any polynomial that has a root modulo every prime
conclusions: one can replace $P(x) = x^2$ in S\'{a}rk\"{o}zy{}'s theorem with any intersective polynomial
nodes.statement_short: Sárközy's theorem holds with $x^2$ replaced by any intersective polynomial (one with a root mod every prime).

nodes.name: Tao-Ziegler asymptotic for polynomial differences in primes
nodes.statement: \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{n \leqslant N} \Lambda(n) \Lambda(n + m^k) = 1 + {\rm o}_{N\to\infty}(1),
assumptions: $M \geqslant \omega(N)N^{1/k}$ for some function $\omega$ going to zero sufficiently slowly depending on $k$
nodes.statement_short: Averaged correlation $\Lambda(n)\Lambda(n+m^k)$ over $m\le M$, $n\le N$ tends to 1.
nodes.label: eqn:tao-ziegler

nodes.name: Piatetski-Shapiro average
nodes.statement: For this we consider a variant of \cref{eqn:tao-ziegler} of the form \begin{equation} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{n \leqslant N} \Lambda(n) \Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \bigr), \end{equation} where $\floor{m^c}$ is a Piatetski-Shapiro sequence for some non-integer $c>2$.
nodes.statement_short: The average of $\Lambda(n)\Lambda(n+\lfloor m^c\rfloor)$ over $m\le M$, $n\le N$, with $\lfloor m^c\rfloor$ a Piatetski-Shapiro sequence, $c>2$ non-integer.

nodes.name: Average along Piatetski-Shapiro sequence
nodes.statement: \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{n \leqslant N} \Lambda(n) \Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \bigr),
nodes.label: eqn:avg

nodes.name: Prime pairs with Piatetski-Shapiro difference
nodes.statement: To our knowledge, averages as in \cref{eqn:avg} have not been considered before, and it is not known whether the primes contain infinitely many pairs whose difference is of the form~$\floor{m^c}$.
nodes.statement_short: Unknown whether infinitely many prime pairs differ by some $\lfloor m^c\rfloor$.

nodes.name: Tao-Ziegler behaviour for fractional powers
nodes.statement: However, based on the heuristic that the map $m \mapsto \floor{m^c}$ nullifies multiplicative structure -- a principle supported by numerous examples in the literature, albeit in different contexts (e.g., \cite{delmer2002}) -- it is natural to conjecture that the average in \cref{eqn:avg} behaves similarly to the Tao-Ziegler case.
assumptions: based on the heuristic that the map $m \mapsto \floor{m^c}$ nullifies multiplicative structure
conclusions: the average in \cref{eqn:avg} behaves similarly to the Tao-Ziegler case
nodes.statement_short: The Piatetski-Shapiro average should behave like the Tao-Ziegler average, i.e. tend to 1.

nodes.name: Main theorem: popular differences along fractional powers
nodes.statement: Let $c > 2$ be a non-integer. For any $A \geqslant 1$ , if $B = \frac{A + 2}{c} $ and $M = \frac{N^{1/c}}{\log^B N}$, then \[ \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{n \leqslant N} \Lambda(n) \Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \bigr) = 1 + {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^A N} \biggr). \]
nodes.statement_short: For non-integer $c>2$ and $M=N^{1/c}/\log^B N$, the average of $\Lambda(n)\Lambda(n+\lfloor m^c\rfloor)$ is $1+O(\log^{-A}N)$.
nodes.label: thm:main-thm

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 1.2
nodes.statement: This theorem immediately implies the following combinatorial corollary.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the main theorem: a positive asymptotic count forces infinitely many pairs.

nodes.name: Infinitely many prime pairs differing by floor(m^c)
nodes.statement: Let $c > 2$ be a non-integer. Then there are infinitely many pairs $(p, m)$ such that $p$ and $p + \floor{m^c}$ are both prime.
conclusions: there are infinitely many pairs $(p, m)$ such that $p$ and $p + \floor{m^c}$ are both prime.
nodes.label: cor:infinitely-many-pairs

nodes.name: Count of prime pairs
nodes.statement: In fact the theorem gives $\approx NM \log^{-2} N$ many such pairs with $p \leqslant N, m \leqslant M$, which is the expected asymptotic if we assume ``independence" of $\Lambda(n)$ and $\Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c}\bigr)$ (see \cref{notation} for the precise meaning of \(\approx\)).
nodes.statement_short: The theorem yields $\approx NM\log^{-2}N$ pairs, the count expected under independence.

nodes.name: Main theorem for all c > 0
nodes.statement: We expect the result to hold with $c > 0$, but this is unproven as of yet.
conclusions: We expect the result to hold with $c > 0$

nodes.name: Trivial case 0 < c < 1
nodes.statement: Note that when $0 < c < 1$, we trivially get infinitely many pairs of primes differing by some integer of the form $\floor{m^c}$, since the image of $\floor{m^c}$ is all positive integers.
nodes.statement_short: For $0<c<1$, $\lfloor m^c\rfloor$ hits every positive integer, so prime pairs exist trivially.

nodes.name: Big-O and little-o notation
nodes.statement: For functions $f, g \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$, $f(x) = {\rm O}\bigl(g(x)\bigr)$ means $\lvert f \rvert \leqslant Cg$ for some constant $C$, and $f(x) = {\rm o}\bigl(g(x)\bigr)$ means $\lvert f/g \rvert \to 0$ as $x \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Vinogradov notation
nodes.statement: We also use the Vinogradov notations $\lesssim$ and $\approx$, where $f \lesssim g$ means $f = {\rm O}(g)$ and $f \approx g$ means $f \lesssim g \lesssim f$.

nodes.name: Floor function
nodes.statement: The notation $\floor{x}$ refers to the floor function, the largest integer $n$ such that $n \leqslant x$.
differentia: the largest integer $n$ such that $n \leqslant x$

nodes.name: Fractional part
nodes.statement: Similarly, the notation $\{x\}$ refers to the fractional part of $x$, given by $x - \floor{x}$.

nodes.name: Cesàro average
nodes.statement: We define the \define{Ces\`{a}ro{} average} of a function $f$ over positive integers $n \leqslant x$ as \begin{equation} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{n \leqslant x} f(n) = \frac{1}{\floor{x}} \sum_{n = 1}^{\floor{x}} f(n). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Cesàro average formula
nodes.statement: \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{n \leqslant x} f(n) = \frac{1}{\floor{x}} \sum_{n = 1}^{\floor{x}} f(n).
nodes.label: def:cesaro

nodes.name: Exponential e(x) and indicator function
nodes.statement: Finally, \(\mathrm{e}(\cdot)\) denotes the function \(\mathrm{e}(x) = e^{2 \pi i x}\) and \(\textbf{1}_{X}(\cdot)\) denotes the indicator function of the set \(X\), i.e., \[ \textbf{1}_{X}(x) = \begin{cases} 1 &\text{if } x \in X\\ \hfil 0 &\text{else} \end{cases}. \]

nodes.name: Discrete Fourier transform
nodes.statement: The \define{discrete Fourier transform} of a function $f \colon \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ is defined for all $\xi \in \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ as \[ \hat{f}(\xi) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}} f(n) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi n}{N} \biggr). \]

nodes.name: Fourier inversion
nodes.statement: Any function $f \colon \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ can be fully recovered from its Fourier coefficients using the formula \[ f(n)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{\xi \in \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}} \hat{f}(\xi) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi n}{N}\biggr). \]
conclusions: can be fully recovered from its Fourier coefficients using the formula
nodes.label: thm:fourier

nodes.name: Parseval's identity
nodes.statement: For any $f \colon \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z} \to\mathbb{C}$, \[ \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}} \lvert f(n) \rvert^2 = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{\xi \in \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}} \bigl\lvert \hat{f}(\xi) \bigr\rvert^2. \]
nodes.label: thm:parseval

nodes.name: von Mangoldt function
nodes.statement: The \define{von Mangoldt function} \(\Lambda \colon \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}\) is given by \[ \Lambda(n) = \begin{cases} \log(p) &\text{if } n = p^k, \text{ where } p \text{ is prime and } k \geqslant 1 \text{ is an integer}\\ \hfil 0 &\text{else} \end{cases}. \] We will denote the Fourier transform of the von Mangoldt function restricted to \(\{1, \ldots, N\}\) and viewed as a function on \(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}\) by \(\hat{\Lambda}\).
nodes.statement_short: $\Lambda(n)=\log p$ if $n=p^k$, else 0; $\hat\Lambda$ is its DFT on $\{1,\dots,N\}$ viewed in $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.label: def:von-mangoldt

nodes.name: Prime Number Theorem (von Mangoldt form)
nodes.statement: We have \[ \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 1}^{N} \Lambda(n) = 1 + {\rm O} \biggl(\frac{1}{e^{t \sqrt{\log N}}} \biggr), \] where $t$ is a positive constant.
nodes.statement_short: The average of $\Lambda$ up to $N$ is $1+O(e^{-t\sqrt{\log N}})$.
nodes.label: thm:prime-number-equiv

nodes.name: Vinogradov's bound for the Fourier transform of the von Mangoldt function
nodes.statement: There exists a constant $C$ such that the following holds: If there exist $q \in \{1, \ldots, N\}$ and $a \in \{0, 1, \ldots, q - 1\}$ such that $\gcd(a,q) = 1$ and $\bigl\lvert \frac{\xi}{N} - \frac{a}{q} \bigr\rvert \leqslant \frac{1}{q^2}$, then \[ \lvert \hat{\Lambda}(\xi) \rvert \leqslant C \biggl(\frac{N}{\sqrt{q}} + N^{\frac{4}{5}} + \sqrt{qN} \biggr) \log^4 N. \]
assumptions: If there exist $q \in \{1, \ldots, N\}$ and $a \in \{0, 1, \ldots, q - 1\}$ such that $\gcd(a,q) = 1$ and $\bigl\lvert \frac{\xi}{N} - \frac{a}{q} \bigr\rvert \leqslant \frac{1}{q^2}$
nodes.statement_short: If $\xi/N$ is within $1/q^2$ of $a/q$, then $|\hat\Lambda(\xi)|\ll (N/\sqrt q+N^{4/5}+\sqrt{qN})\log^4N$.
nodes.label: thm:vinogradov

nodes.name: Erdős-Turán inequality
nodes.statement: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on the unit circle \(S^1\). Then, for any natural number \(K\), \[ \sup_{A} \lvert \mu (A) - \mathrm{Leb}(A)\rvert \leqslant 10 \Biggl( \frac{1}{K} + \sum_{k=1}^{K} \frac{\bigl\lvert \hat{\mu} (k) \bigr\rvert}{k} \Biggr), \] where the supremum is over all arcs \(A \subseteq S^1\) of the unit circle, \(\mathrm{Leb}\) is the Lebesgue measure, and \(\hat{\mu}(k)\) is the discrete Fourier transform of $\mu$ evaluated at \(k\).
assumptions: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on the unit circle \(S^1\).
nodes.statement_short: Discrepancy of a probability measure on the circle is bounded by $1/K$ plus its first $K$ Fourier coefficients.
nodes.label: thm:erdos-turan

nodes.name: Poulias's bound on a Diophantine inequality
nodes.statement: If $c > 2$ and \[ 2k > \bigl(\floor{2c} + 1 \bigr) \bigl(\floor{2c} + 2 \bigr) + 1, \] then the number of solutions to \[ \lvert m_1^c + \cdots + m_k^c - m_{k + 1}^c - \cdots - m_{2k}^c \rvert \leqslant k \] in the interval $[1, M]^{2k}$ is $\lesssim M^{2k - c}$, where the implied constant depends on $c$ and $k$, but not on $M$.
conclusions: in the interval $[1, M]^{2k}$ is $\lesssim M^{2k - c}$
nodes.statement_short: For $c>2$ and $k$ large, $|\sum_{i\le k} m_i^c-\sum_{i>k} m_i^c|\le k$ has $\lesssim M^{2k-c}$ solutions in $[1,M]^{2k}$.
nodes.label: thm:poulias

nodes.name: Graham-Kolesnik van der Corput estimate
nodes.statement: Let $q$ be a non-negative integer and $f$ be a function with $q + 2$ continuous derivatives on the interval $I \subseteq [X, 2X]$. Assume that there are constants $B_1, B_2$, and $F$ such that \begin{equation} B_1 F X^{-r} \leqslant \lvert f^{(r)}(x)\rvert \leqslant B_2 F X^{-r} \end{equation} for all $1 \leqslant r \leqslant q + 2$. Then there is a constant $B = B(B_1,B_2)$ such that \[ \biggl\lvert \sum_{n \in I} \mathrm{e}\bigl(f(n) \bigr) \biggr\rvert \leqslant B \biggl(F^\frac{1}{2^{q+2}-2}X^{1-\frac{q+2}{2^{q+2}-2}} + \frac{X}{F} \biggr). \]

nodes.label: thm:vdc-estimate

nodes.statement: B_1 F X^{-r} \leqslant \lvert f^{(r)}(x)\rvert \leqslant B_2 F X^{-r}

nodes.name: Outline of the proof of the main theorem
nodes.statement: Our argument is Fourier-analytic in nature. Initially we recast the averages \eqref{eqn:avg} in terms of Fourier transforms. Consequently, the main term (which equals $1$) comes from the trivial character, while the rest of the characters are divided into two disjoint parts. In the first part (treating the case where the character is ``close" to one), we use the combination of an elementary argument using the Prime Number Theorem and Vinogradov's bounds for $\hat{\Lambda}$, depending on whether the character is ``too close" to one or not, and Poulias's bound for the number of solutions to a Diophantine inequality for the other term involving an exponential sum. In the second part, we estimate $\hat{\Lambda}$ trivially and use the Erd\H{o}s-Tur{\'a}n{} inequality to convert the exponential sum involving $\floor{m^c}$ to one involving $m^c$, then use van der Corput estimates for this new sum, which can be applied because of the smoothness of the function $m^c$. Putting everything together, this proves the result.
nodes.statement_short: Fourier-analytic sketch: split characters into trivial, close and far; bound via PNT/Vinogradov/Poulias and Erdős-Turán/van der Corput.

nodes.name: Recast in Fourier terms
nodes.statement: Our argument is Fourier-analytic in nature. Initially we recast the averages \eqref{eqn:avg} in terms of Fourier transforms. Consequently, the main term (which equals $1$) comes from the trivial character, while the rest of the characters are divided into two disjoint parts.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the average via Fourier transforms; the trivial character gives the main term 1.

nodes.statement_short: Close characters: PNT, Vinogradov bounds and Poulias's count.

Putting everything together, this proves the result.
nodes.statement_short: Far characters: Erdős-Turán to remove the floor, then van der Corput.

nodes.name: Fourier expansion of the Piatetski-Shapiro average
nodes.statement: Let $N\in \mathbb{N}$, $c > 2$ be a non-integer, $B \geqslant \frac{3}{c}$, and $M = \frac{N^{1/c}}{\log^{B} N}$. Then \[ \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{n \leqslant N} \Lambda(n) \Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \bigr) = \frac{1}{N^2} \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \bigl\lvert \hat{\Lambda}(\xi) \bigr\rvert^2 \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} \floor{m^c} \!\biggr) + {\rm O} \biggl(\frac{1}{\log^{Bc-2}{N}}\biggr). \]
assumptions: Let $N\in \mathbb{N}$, $c > 2$ be a non-integer, $B \geqslant \frac{3}{c}$, and $M = \frac{N^{1/c}}{\log^{B} N}$.
nodes.statement_short: The average equals $N^{-2}\sum_\xi|\hat\Lambda(\xi)|^2\,\mathbb{E}_m e(-\xi\lfloor m^c\rfloor/N)$ up to $O(\log^{2-Bc}N)$.
nodes.label: prop:fourier-transform

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.10
nodes.statement: First, unpacking notation yields \begin{equation} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{n \leqslant N} \Lambda(n) \Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \bigr) = \frac{1}{NM} \sum_{m = 0}^{M - 1} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) \Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \bigr). \end{equation} We next apply the Fourier inversion formula (\cref{thm:fourier}) to each of the indicator functions in the above right-hand side. To allow us to do so, we shift the domains of \(\Lambda(n)\) and \(\Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \bigr)\) to \(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}\) by taking the arguments modulo \(N\): \begin{equation*} \eqref{eqn:just-by-definition} = \frac{1}{NM} \sum_{m = 0}^{M - 1} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda\bigl(n \text{ (mod } N) \bigr) \Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \text{ (mod } N)\bigr) + {\rm O} \biggl(\frac{M^c}{N} \log^2{N} \biggr). \end{equation*} This transformation introduces an error of \({\rm O} \bigl((M^c/N)\log^2{N} \bigr)\) because the difference between \(\Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \bigr)\) and \(\Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \text{ (mod } N) \bigr)\) is $\lesssim \log N$, and $\Lambda\bigl(n\text{ (mod } N) \bigr) = \Lambda(n) \lesssim \log N$. Now, \begin{align*} \begin{split} \eqref{eqn:just-by-definition} &= \frac{1}{NM} \sum_{m = 0}^{M - 1} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Biggl(\frac{1}{N} \sum_{\eta = 0}^{N - 1} \hat{\Lambda}(\eta) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\eta}{N} n \biggr) \Biggr)\\ &\hphantom{= \frac{1}{NM} \sum_{m = 0}^{M - 1} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1}}\ \cdot \Biggl(\frac{1}{N} \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \hat{\Lambda}(\xi) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} \bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \bigr) \biggr) \Biggr) + {\rm O} \biggl(\frac{M^c}{N}\log^2{N} \biggr) \end{split}\\ \begin{split} &= \frac{1}{N^2M} \sum_{m = 0}^{M - 1} \, \sum_{\eta,\, \xi = 0}^{N - 1} \hat{\Lambda}(\xi)\hat{\Lambda}(\eta) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} \floor{m^c} \!\biggr)\\ &\hphantom{= \frac{1}{NM} \sum_{m = 0}^{M - 1} \, \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1}}\ \cdot \Biggl(\frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi + \eta}{N} n \biggr)\Biggr) + {\rm O} \biggl(\frac{M^c}{N}\log^2{N} \biggr). \end{split} \end{align*} Note that \(\sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \mathrm{e}\bigl(-n(\xi + \eta)/N \bigr) = 0\) unless \(\eta +\xi = N\). So, all of the cross terms cancel, and we are left with the simpler sum \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{n \leqslant N} \Lambda(n) \Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \!\bigr) &= \frac{1}{N^2M} \sum_{m = 0}^{M - 1} \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \bigl\lvert \hat{\Lambda}(\xi) \bigr\rvert^2 \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} \floor{m^c} \!\biggr) + {\rm O} \biggl(\frac{M^c}{N}\log^2{N} \biggr)\\ &=\frac{1}{N^2} \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \bigl\lvert \hat{\Lambda}(\xi) \bigr\rvert^2 \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} \floor{m^c} \!\biggr) + {\rm O} \biggl(\frac{1}{\log^{Bc-2}{N}}\biggr), \end{align*} where in the first step we used that $\hat{\Lambda}(\xi) = \overline{\hat{\Lambda}(-\xi)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Unpack the average, reduce arguments mod $N$, apply Fourier inversion and orthogonality of characters.

nodes.name: Unpacked average
nodes.statement: \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{n \leqslant N} \Lambda(n) \Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \bigr) = \frac{1}{NM} \sum_{m = 0}^{M - 1} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) \Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \bigr).
nodes.label: eqn:just-by-definition

nodes.name: Unpack notation
nodes.statement: First, unpacking notation yields \begin{equation} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{n \leqslant N} \Lambda(n) \Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \bigr) = \frac{1}{NM} \sum_{m = 0}^{M - 1} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) \Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \bigr). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Write the average as an explicit double sum.

nodes.name: Reduce modulo N
nodes.statement: We next apply the Fourier inversion formula (\cref{thm:fourier}) to each of the indicator functions in the above right-hand side. To allow us to do so, we shift the domains of \(\Lambda(n)\) and \(\Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \bigr)\) to \(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}\) by taking the arguments modulo \(N\): \begin{equation*} \eqref{eqn:just-by-definition} = \frac{1}{NM} \sum_{m = 0}^{M - 1} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda\bigl(n \text{ (mod } N) \bigr) \Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \text{ (mod } N)\bigr) + {\rm O} \biggl(\frac{M^c}{N} \log^2{N} \biggr). \end{equation*} This transformation introduces an error of \({\rm O} \bigl((M^c/N)\log^2{N} \bigr)\) because the difference between \(\Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \bigr)\) and \(\Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \text{ (mod } N) \bigr)\) is $\lesssim \log N$, and $\Lambda\bigl(n\text{ (mod } N) \bigr) = \Lambda(n) \lesssim \log N$.
nodes.statement_short: Move to $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ at cost $O((M^c/N)\log^2N)$.

nodes.name: Apply Fourier inversion
nodes.statement: Now, \begin{align*} \begin{split} \eqref{eqn:just-by-definition} &= \frac{1}{NM} \sum_{m = 0}^{M - 1} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Biggl(\frac{1}{N} \sum_{\eta = 0}^{N - 1} \hat{\Lambda}(\eta) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\eta}{N} n \biggr) \Biggr)\\ &\hphantom{= \frac{1}{NM} \sum_{m = 0}^{M - 1} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1}}\ \cdot \Biggl(\frac{1}{N} \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \hat{\Lambda}(\xi) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} \bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \bigr) \biggr) \Biggr) + {\rm O} \biggl(\frac{M^c}{N}\log^2{N} \biggr) \end{split}\\ \begin{split} &= \frac{1}{N^2M} \sum_{m = 0}^{M - 1} \, \sum_{\eta,\, \xi = 0}^{N - 1} \hat{\Lambda}(\xi)\hat{\Lambda}(\eta) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} \floor{m^c} \!\biggr)\\ &\hphantom{= \frac{1}{NM} \sum_{m = 0}^{M - 1} \, \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1}}\ \cdot \Biggl(\frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi + \eta}{N} n \biggr)\Biggr) + {\rm O} \biggl(\frac{M^c}{N}\log^2{N} \biggr). \end{split} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand both $\Lambda$ factors by Fourier inversion.

nodes.name: Orthogonality
nodes.statement: Note that \(\sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \mathrm{e}\bigl(-n(\xi + \eta)/N \bigr) = 0\) unless \(\eta +\xi = N\). So, all of the cross terms cancel, and we are left with the simpler sum \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{n \leqslant N} \Lambda(n) \Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{m^c} \!\bigr) &= \frac{1}{N^2M} \sum_{m = 0}^{M - 1} \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \bigl\lvert \hat{\Lambda}(\xi) \bigr\rvert^2 \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} \floor{m^c} \!\biggr) + {\rm O} \biggl(\frac{M^c}{N}\log^2{N} \biggr)\\ &=\frac{1}{N^2} \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \bigl\lvert \hat{\Lambda}(\xi) \bigr\rvert^2 \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} \floor{m^c} \!\biggr) + {\rm O} \biggl(\frac{1}{\log^{Bc-2}{N}}\biggr), \end{align*} where in the first step we used that $\hat{\Lambda}(\xi) = \overline{\hat{\Lambda}(-\xi)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Cross terms vanish by orthogonality, leaving the $|\hat\Lambda|^2$ sum.

nodes.name: Reduction of the main theorem to Theorem 3.1
nodes.statement: In view of \cref{prop:fourier-transform}, the following directly implies \cref{thm:main-thm}.
nodes.statement_short: Main theorem follows from Proposition 2.10 combined with Theorem 3.1.

nodes.name: Fourier-side asymptotic for c > 2
nodes.statement: Let $c > 2$ be a non-integer. For any $A \geqslant 1$ there exists $B \geqslant 1$ such that if $M = \frac{N^{1/c}}{\log^{B} N}$, then \[ \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2 \Biggl(\frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^M \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\Biggr) = 1 + {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^A N} \biggr). \]
nodes.statement_short: The weighted Fourier sum $\sum_\xi|\hat\Lambda(\xi)/N|^2\,\mathbb{E}_m e(-\xi\lfloor m^c\rfloor/N)$ equals $1+O(\log^{-A}N)$.
nodes.label: thm:c-greater-than-2

nodes.name: Parameters b and k
nodes.statement: Let $b = 4kA + 2Bc + 4k$, where $k = \ceil*{\bigl((\floor{2c} + 1)(\floor{2c} + 2) + 1 \bigr)/2}$, as in \cref{thm:poulias}.

nodes.name: Sums Sigma_1 and Sigma_2
nodes.statement: We can write \begin{equation} \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2 \Biggl(\frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^M \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\Biggr) = \biggl(\frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 1}^N \Lambda(n) \biggr)^2 + \Sigma_1 + \Sigma_2, \end{equation} where \begin{align*} \Sigma_1 &= \sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2 \Biggl(\frac{1}{M} \sum_{m=1}^M \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\Biggr)\\ \intertext{and} \Sigma_2 &= \mkern-10mu \sum_{\xi = \frac{N}{\log^b N}}^{\frac{N}{2}} \!\! \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2 \Biggl(\frac{1}{M} \sum_{m=1}^M \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\Biggr). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Split the Fourier sum into the $\xi=0$ term, $\Sigma_1$ ($1\le\xi\le N/\log^bN$) and $\Sigma_2$ ($N/\log^bN\le\xi\le N/2$).

nodes.name: Decomposition of the main sum
nodes.statement: \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2 \Biggl(\frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^M \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\Biggr) = \biggl(\frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 1}^N \Lambda(n) \biggr)^2 + \Sigma_1 + \Sigma_2,
nodes.label: eqn:main-sum-decomp

nodes.name: Reduction of Theorem 3.1 to Propositions 3.2 and 3.3
nodes.statement: Since $\lvert \hat{\Lambda}(\xi) \rvert = \lvert \hat{\Lambda}(-\xi) \rvert$, we can reduce to the case where $\xi \leqslant N/2$. Furthermore, since $\frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 1}^{N} \Lambda(n) = 1 + {\rm O} \bigl(e^{-t \sqrt{\log N}} \bigr)$ (\cref{thm:prime-number-equiv}) and $e^{-t \sqrt{\log N}}$ decays faster than $\log^{-k} N$ for any $k$, it suffices to show the following propositions by \cref{eqn:main-sum-decomp}.
nodes.statement_short: By symmetry and the PNT, Theorem 3.1 reduces via (3.1) to bounding $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$.

nodes.name: Estimate for Sigma_1
nodes.statement: For any \(A \geqslant 1\), \[ \Sigma_1 = {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^A N} \biggr). \]
nodes.label: prop:estimate-sigma1

nodes.name: Estimate for Sigma_2
nodes.statement: For any \(A \geqslant 1\), \[ \Sigma_2 = {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^A N} \biggr). \]
nodes.label: prop:estimate-sigma2

nodes.name: Main theorem from Propositions 3.2 and 3.3
nodes.statement: Combining \cref{prop:estimate-sigma1} and \cref{prop:estimate-sigma2} gives \cref{thm:main-thm}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the bounds on $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$.

nodes.name: Proof idea for Proposition 3.2
nodes.statement: The idea is as follows (it might help to read this paragraph in conjunction with the proof of \cref{prop:estimate-sigma1} at the end of the section): Parseval's identity provides good bounds for the sum of $\lvert \hat{\Lambda} \rvert^2$, and the even power sums of the sum of $\mathrm{e}(-\xi \floor{m^c}/N)$ have an obvious interpretation as the number of solutions to a Diophantine equation. So, we decouple the $\hat{\Lambda}$ sum from the $\mathrm{e}(-\xi \floor{m^c}/N)$ sum to deal with them separately. In order to decouple, we need to apply H\"{o}lder's inequality, but in doing so the exponent of 2 on $\hat{\Lambda}$ changes. To account for this, we rewrite the exponent as $2 = 1/k + (2 - 1/k)$ and factor out the maximum of the first summand. This leaves us to deal with the maximum value of $\hat{\Lambda}$ and bound the number of solutions to a Diophantine equation.
nodes.statement_short: Sketch: decouple $\hat\Lambda$ and exponential sums by Hölder, then use Parseval, a sup bound on $\hat\Lambda$ and a Diophantine count.

nodes.name: Two tools
nodes.statement: The idea is as follows (it might help to read this paragraph in conjunction with the proof of \cref{prop:estimate-sigma1} at the end of the section): Parseval's identity provides good bounds for the sum of $\lvert \hat{\Lambda} \rvert^2$, and the even power sums of the sum of $\mathrm{e}(-\xi \floor{m^c}/N)$ have an obvious interpretation as the number of solutions to a Diophantine equation.
nodes.statement_short: Parseval controls $|\hat\Lambda|^2$; even moments of the exponential sum count Diophantine solutions.

nodes.name: Decouple
nodes.statement: So, we decouple the $\hat{\Lambda}$ sum from the $\mathrm{e}(-\xi \floor{m^c}/N)$ sum to deal with them separately.
nodes.statement_short: Separate the two sums.

nodes.name: Hölder with split exponent
nodes.statement: In order to decouple, we need to apply H\"{o}lder's inequality, but in doing so the exponent of 2 on $\hat{\Lambda}$ changes. To account for this, we rewrite the exponent as $2 = 1/k + (2 - 1/k)$ and factor out the maximum of the first summand.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Hölder after writing $2=1/k+(2-1/k)$ and factoring out a maximum.

nodes.name: Remaining tasks
nodes.statement: This leaves us to deal with the maximum value of $\hat{\Lambda}$ and bound the number of solutions to a Diophantine equation.
nodes.statement_short: Remains: sup of $\hat\Lambda$ and a Diophantine solution count.

nodes.name: Second moment bound for Lambda-hat
nodes.statement: For any $b \geqslant 1$ and any $k \geqslant 1$ the following holds: \[ \Biggl(\sum_{\xi = 1}^{\log^b N} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^{2} \Biggr)^{1-\frac{1}{2k}} \mkern-32mu = {\rm O}(\log N). \]
nodes.statement_short: The (partial) second moment of $\hat\Lambda/N$, raised to $1-1/(2k)$, is $O(\log N)$.
nodes.label: lem:parseval-bound

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.4
nodes.statement: We have \begin{equation*} \sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^{2} \leqslant \sum_{\xi = 1}^{N} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^{2} \! = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{\xi = 1}^{N} \bigl(\Lambda(\xi)\bigr)^2, \end{equation*} where the equality holds by Parseval's identity (\cref{thm:parseval}). Now, \begin{equation*} \frac{1}{N} \sum_{\xi = 1}^{N} \bigl(\Lambda(\xi)\bigr)^2 \leqslant \frac{1}{N} \biggl(\sum_{\xi = 1}^{N} \Lambda(\xi) \biggr) \max_{\xi} \Lambda(\xi) \leqslant \frac{1}{N} \biggl(\sum_{\xi = 1}^{N} \Lambda(\xi) \biggr) \log N. \end{equation*} By the Prime Number Theorem, $\displaystyle \lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{1}{N} \biggl(\sum_{\xi = 1}^{N} \Lambda(\xi) \biggr) = 1$ and the result follows.
nodes.statement_short: Extend the sum, apply Parseval, bound $\Lambda\le\log N$ and use the Prime Number Theorem.

nodes.name: Apply Parseval
nodes.statement: We have \begin{equation*} \sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^{2} \leqslant \sum_{\xi = 1}^{N} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^{2} \! = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{\xi = 1}^{N} \bigl(\Lambda(\xi)\bigr)^2, \end{equation*} where the equality holds by Parseval's identity (\cref{thm:parseval}).
nodes.statement_short: Extend to the full sum and apply Parseval.

nodes.name: Bound by log N
nodes.statement: Now, \begin{equation*} \frac{1}{N} \sum_{\xi = 1}^{N} \bigl(\Lambda(\xi)\bigr)^2 \leqslant \frac{1}{N} \biggl(\sum_{\xi = 1}^{N} \Lambda(\xi) \biggr) \max_{\xi} \Lambda(\xi) \leqslant \frac{1}{N} \biggl(\sum_{\xi = 1}^{N} \Lambda(\xi) \biggr) \log N. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\Lambda^2\le\Lambda\log N$.

nodes.name: Apply PNT
nodes.statement: By the Prime Number Theorem, $\displaystyle \lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{1}{N} \biggl(\sum_{\xi = 1}^{N} \Lambda(\xi) \biggr) = 1$ and the result follows.
nodes.statement_short: PNT gives average of $\Lambda$ tending to 1.

nodes.name: Vinogradov-range bound on Lambda-hat
nodes.statement: Suppose $b\geqslant 16$. The following holds: \[ \sup_{\mathclap{\log^b N < \xi \leqslant \frac{N}{\log^b N}}}\; \bigl\lvert \hat{\Lambda}(\xi) \bigr\rvert = {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{N}{\log^{\frac{b}{4}} N} \biggr). \]
nodes.statement_short: For $\log^bN<\xi\le N/\log^bN$, $|\hat\Lambda(\xi)|=O(N/\log^{b/4}N)$.
nodes.label: lem:rational-approx-bound

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.5
nodes.statement: First, observe that $\displaystyle \lim_{N \to \infty} \biggl(\frac{1}{\log^{\frac{b}{2}} N} + \frac{\log^b N}{N} \biggr) = 0$. Therefore, there exists $N_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that, for all \(N \geqslant N_0\), \[ \frac{N}{\log^{\frac{b}{2}} N} + \log^b N < N. \] Suppose that $N \geqslant N_0$ and $\xi \in (\log^b N, N/\log^b N]$. By Dirichlet's approximation theorem, we can find $a \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $q \leqslant N/\log^b N$ such that $\gcd(a, q) = 1$ and \[ \biggl\lvert\frac{\xi}{N} - \frac{a}{q} \biggr\rvert \leqslant \frac{1}{\frac{N}{\log^b N} q} \leqslant \frac{1}{q^2}. \] Clearing denominators, the first inequality gives us \(\lvert q\xi - aN \rvert \leqslant \log^b N\), meaning \(q\xi \geqslant aN - \log^b N\). If \(a = 0\), then $\lvert q\xi \rvert \leqslant \log^b N$. However, by our choice of \(\xi\), $\log^b N < q\xi$, a contradiction. Thus, \(a \neq 0\), and \begin{equation*} q\xi \geqslant aN - \log^b N \geqslant N - \log^b N. \end{equation*} Now, aiming for another contradiction, assume that $q \leqslant \log^{b/2} N$. As such, \begin{equation*} q\xi \leqslant (\log^{\frac{b}{2}} N) \frac{N}{\log^b N} = \frac{N}{\log^{\frac{b}{2}} N}. \end{equation*} Rearranging terms gives us that \begin{equation*} N - \log^b N \leqslant \frac{N}{\log^{\frac{b}{2}} N}. \end{equation*} However, by hypothesis, \(N > (N/\log^{b/2} N) + \log^b N\), which yields a contradiction. Therefore, $q > \log^{b/2} N$. Next, applying Vinogradov's theorem (\cref{thm:vinogradov}) gives us \begin{align*} \biggl\lvert \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N}n \biggr) \biggr\rvert &\leqslant C \biggl(\frac{N}{\sqrt{q}} + N^{\frac{4}{5}} + \sqrt{qN} \biggr) \log^4 N\\ &\leqslant C \biggl(\frac{N}{\log^{\frac{b}{4}} N} + N^{\frac{4}{5}} + \frac{N}{\log^{\frac{b}{2}} N} \biggr) \log^4 N.\\ \intertext{Thus, since the above holds for all $\xi \in (\log^b N, N/\log^b N]$,} \sup_{\mathclap{\log^b N < \xi \leqslant \frac{N}{\log^b N}}}\; \bigl\lvert \hat{\Lambda}(\xi) \bigr\rvert &\leqslant C \biggl(\frac{N}{\log^{\frac{b}{4}} N} + N^{\frac{4}{5}} +\frac{N}{\log^{\frac{b}{2} - 4} N}\biggr)\\ \intertext{for all $N \geqslant N_0$. Therefore,} \sup_{\mathclap{\log^b N < \xi \leqslant \frac{N}{\log^b N}}}\; \bigl\lvert \hat{\Lambda}(\xi) \bigr\rvert &= {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{N}{\log^{\frac{b}{4}} N} \biggr), \end{align*} since, if $b \geqslant 16$, then $b/2 - 4 \geqslant b/4$.
nodes.statement_short: Dirichlet approximation of $\xi/N$ with denominator $q>\log^{b/2}N$ (by contradiction), then Vinogradov's bound.

nodes.name: Choose N_0
nodes.statement: First, observe that $\displaystyle \lim_{N \to \infty} \biggl(\frac{1}{\log^{\frac{b}{2}} N} + \frac{\log^b N}{N} \biggr) = 0$. Therefore, there exists $N_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that, for all \(N \geqslant N_0\), \[ \frac{N}{\log^{\frac{b}{2}} N} + \log^b N < N. \]
nodes.statement_short: Fix $N_0$ beyond which $N/\log^{b/2}N+\log^bN<N$.

nodes.name: Dirichlet approximation
nodes.statement: Suppose that $N \geqslant N_0$ and $\xi \in (\log^b N, N/\log^b N]$. By Dirichlet's approximation theorem, we can find $a \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $q \leqslant N/\log^b N$ such that $\gcd(a, q) = 1$ and \[ \biggl\lvert\frac{\xi}{N} - \frac{a}{q} \biggr\rvert \leqslant \frac{1}{\frac{N}{\log^b N} q} \leqslant \frac{1}{q^2}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Dirichlet gives $a/q$ with $q\le N/\log^bN$ approximating $\xi/N$.

nodes.name: a is nonzero
nodes.statement: Clearing denominators, the first inequality gives us \(\lvert q\xi - aN \rvert \leqslant \log^b N\), meaning \(q\xi \geqslant aN - \log^b N\). If \(a = 0\), then $\lvert q\xi \rvert \leqslant \log^b N$. However, by our choice of \(\xi\), $\log^b N < q\xi$, a contradiction. Thus, \(a \neq 0\), and \begin{equation*} q\xi \geqslant aN - \log^b N \geqslant N - \log^b N. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: $a=0$ contradicts $\xi>\log^bN$, so $q\xi\ge N-\log^bN$.

nodes.name: q is large
nodes.statement: Now, aiming for another contradiction, assume that $q \leqslant \log^{b/2} N$. As such, \begin{equation*} q\xi \leqslant (\log^{\frac{b}{2}} N) \frac{N}{\log^b N} = \frac{N}{\log^{\frac{b}{2}} N}. \end{equation*} Rearranging terms gives us that \begin{equation*} N - \log^b N \leqslant \frac{N}{\log^{\frac{b}{2}} N}. \end{equation*} However, by hypothesis, \(N > (N/\log^{b/2} N) + \log^b N\), which yields a contradiction. Therefore, $q > \log^{b/2} N$.
nodes.statement_short: Assuming $q\le\log^{b/2}N$ contradicts the choice of $N_0$.

nodes.name: Apply Vinogradov
nodes.statement: Next, applying Vinogradov's theorem (\cref{thm:vinogradov}) gives us \begin{align*} \biggl\lvert \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N}n \biggr) \biggr\rvert &\leqslant C \biggl(\frac{N}{\sqrt{q}} + N^{\frac{4}{5}} + \sqrt{qN} \biggr) \log^4 N\\ &\leqslant C \biggl(\frac{N}{\log^{\frac{b}{4}} N} + N^{\frac{4}{5}} + \frac{N}{\log^{\frac{b}{2}} N} \biggr) \log^4 N.\\ \intertext{Thus, since the above holds for all $\xi \in (\log^b N, N/\log^b N]$,} \sup_{\mathclap{\log^b N < \xi \leqslant \frac{N}{\log^b N}}}\; \bigl\lvert \hat{\Lambda}(\xi) \bigr\rvert &\leqslant C \biggl(\frac{N}{\log^{\frac{b}{4}} N} + N^{\frac{4}{5}} +\frac{N}{\log^{\frac{b}{2} - 4} N}\biggr)\\ \intertext{for all $N \geqslant N_0$. Therefore,} \sup_{\mathclap{\log^b N < \xi \leqslant \frac{N}{\log^b N}}}\; \bigl\lvert \hat{\Lambda}(\xi) \bigr\rvert &= {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{N}{\log^{\frac{b}{4}} N} \biggr), \end{align*} since, if $b \geqslant 16$, then $b/2 - 4 \geqslant b/4$.
nodes.statement_short: Vinogradov's bound with $q>\log^{b/2}N$ gives the claim for $b\ge16$.

nodes.name: Small-frequency bound on Lambda-hat
nodes.statement: For any $b, m \geqslant 1$, \[ \sup_{1 \leqslant \xi \leqslant \log^b N} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} n \biggr)\biggr\rvert = {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^m N} \biggr). \]
nodes.statement_short: For $1\le\xi\le\log^bN$, $|\hat\Lambda(\xi)|/N=O(\log^{-m}N)$.
nodes.label: lem:small-xi-bound

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.6
nodes.statement_short: Approximate $e(\cdot)$ by step functions $f_k$ and use the PNT on short intervals. The key step bounds each interval's $\Lambda$-mass by $1/(rk)$ up to $e^{-t\sqrt{\log}}$ errors.

nodes.name: Step-function approximation error
nodes.statement: \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) \mathrm{e}\Bigl(\frac{\xi}{N} n \Bigr) \biggr\rvert &\leqslant \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) f_k\Bigl(\frac{\xi}{N} n \Bigr) \biggr\rvert + \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) \biggl(\mathrm{e}\Bigl(\frac{\xi}{N} n \Bigr) - f_k\Bigl(\frac{\xi}{N} n \Bigr)\biggr)\biggr\rvert \nonumber\\ &\leqslant \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) f_k\Bigl(\frac{\xi}{N} n \Bigr) \biggr\rvert + \frac{2\pi}{kN} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n),
nodes.label: eqn:from-N-big

nodes.name: Rewriting with step functions
nodes.statement: \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) f_k\Bigl(\frac{rn}{N} \Bigr) \biggr\rvert = \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{\xi = 0}^{rk - 1} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{k} \biggr) \; \cdot \; \smashoperator{\sum_{\mkern26mu \frac{\xi N}{rk} \leqslant n < \frac{(\xi + 1) N}{rk}}} \Lambda(n) \biggr\rvert.
nodes.label: eqn:restricting-xi

nodes.name: Bound on restricted sum
nodes.label: eqn:bounding-restricted-xi

nodes.name: PNT error
nodes.statement: By the Prime Number Theorem (\cref{thm:prime-number-equiv}), there exist $N_1 \in \mathbb{N}, C, t > 0$ such that \begin{equation*} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) - 1 \biggr\rvert \leqslant \frac{C}{e^{t\sqrt{\log N}}} \end{equation*} for all \(N \geqslant N_1\).
nodes.statement_short: PNT with explicit error for $N\ge N_1$.

nodes.name: Choose N_2
nodes.statement: Now, since $\displaystyle \lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{N}{\log^{m+b} N} = \infty$, there exists $N_2 \in \mathbb{N}$ so that, for all \(N \geqslant N_2\), \[ \frac{N}{\log^{m + b} N} \geqslant N_1. \]
nodes.statement_short: Fix $N_2$ so $N/\log^{m+b}N\ge N_1$.

nodes.name: Choose N_3
nodes.statement: Further, it can be verified that \begin{equation*} \lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{2C\log^{m + b} N}{e^{t \sqrt{\log \frac{N}{\log^{m + b} N}}}} = 0, \end{equation*} so we can find $N_3 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that, for all \(N \geqslant N_3\), \begin{equation*} \frac{2C\log^{m + b} N}{e^{t \sqrt{\log \frac{N}{\log^{m + b} N}}}} \leqslant \frac{1}{\log^m N}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Fix $N_3$ so the PNT error times $\log^{m+b}N$ is below $\log^{-m}N$.

nodes.name: Step-function approximation
nodes.statement: With the above in mind, suppose $N \geqslant \max\{N_2, N_3\}$ and let $k = \floor{\log^m N}$. Accordingly, \begin{align} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) \mathrm{e}\Bigl(\frac{\xi}{N} n \Bigr) \biggr\rvert &\leqslant \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) f_k\Bigl(\frac{\xi}{N} n \Bigr) \biggr\rvert + \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) \biggl(\mathrm{e}\Bigl(\frac{\xi}{N} n \Bigr) - f_k\Bigl(\frac{\xi}{N} n \Bigr)\biggr)\biggr\rvert \nonumber\\ &\leqslant \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) f_k\Bigl(\frac{\xi}{N} n \Bigr) \biggr\rvert + \frac{2\pi}{kN} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n), \end{align} where $f_k \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ is the function satisfying $f_k(x) = \mathrm{e}\bigl(\floor{kx}/k \bigr)$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $k=\lfloor\log^mN\rfloor$ and $f_k$; bound the error of replacing $e$ by $f_k$.

nodes.name: Group into intervals
nodes.statement: \cref{eqn:from-N-big} holds for all $\xi \in [0, N - 1]$. Suppose \(r \in \mathbb{N}\) such that $1 \leqslant r \leqslant \log^b N$. Then, \begin{equation} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) f_k\Bigl(\frac{rn}{N} \Bigr) \biggr\rvert = \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{\xi = 0}^{rk - 1} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{k} \biggr) \; \cdot \; \smashoperator{\sum_{\mkern26mu \frac{\xi N}{rk} \leqslant n < \frac{(\xi + 1) N}{rk}}} \Lambda(n) \biggr\rvert. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the $f_k$-sum as a sum over $rk$ intervals.

nodes.name: Interval masses via PNT
nodes.statement: Further, for each $\xi = 0, 1, \ldots, rk - 1$, \begin{align*} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{N} \; \cdot \; \smashoperator{\sum_{\mkern26mu \frac{\xi N}{rk} \leqslant n < \frac{(\xi + 1)N}{rk}}} \Lambda(n) - \frac{1}{rk} \biggr\rvert &= \Biggl\lvert \biggl(\frac{\frac{\xi + 1}{rk}}{\frac{(\xi + 1)N}{rk}} \:\smashoperator{\sum_{\mkern14mu n < \frac{(\xi + 1)N}{{rk}}}} \Lambda(n) - \frac{\xi + 1}{rk} \biggr) - \biggl(\frac{\frac{\xi}{rk}}{\frac{\xi N}{rk}} \:\smashoperator{\sum_{\, n < \frac{\xi N}{rk}}} \Lambda(n) - \frac{\xi}{rk} \biggr)\Biggr\rvert\\ &\leqslant \frac{\xi + 1}{rk} \Biggl\lvert \frac{1}{\frac{(\xi + 1)N}{rk}} \:\smashoperator{\sum_{\mkern14mu n < \frac{(\xi + 1)N}{{rk}}}} \Lambda(n) - 1 \Biggr\rvert + \frac{\xi}{rk} \Biggl\lvert \frac{1}{\frac{\xi N}{rk}} \:\smashoperator{\sum_{\, n < \frac{\xi N}{rk}}} \Lambda(n) - 1 \Biggr\rvert\\ &\leqslant \frac{2C}{e^{t\sqrt{\log \frac{\xi N}{rk}}}}, \end{align*} because if $\xi \geqslant 1$, then \begin{equation*} \frac{\xi N}{rk} \geqslant \frac{N}{\log^{m + b} N}\geqslant N_1. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Each interval's $\Lambda$-mass is $1/(rk)$ up to PNT error.

nodes.name: Bound restricted sum
nodes.statement_short: The main parts cancel; the errors sum to at most $\log^{-m}N$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: By \cref{eqn:from-N-big}, \cref{eqn:restricting-xi}, and \cref{eqn:bounding-restricted-xi}, we obtain that, for any $\xi \in [1, \log^b N]$, \begin{align*} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} n \biggr) \biggr\rvert &\leqslant \frac{1}{\log^m N} + \frac{2\pi}{kN} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n).\\ \intertext{Therefore, for all \(N \geqslant \max\{N_2, N_3\}\),} \sup_{1 \leqslant \xi \leqslant \log^b N} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} n \biggr) \biggr\rvert &\leqslant \frac{1}{\log^m N} + \frac{2\pi}{kN} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n).\\ \intertext{So,} \sup_{1\leqslant \xi \leqslant \log^b N} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(n) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} n \biggr) \biggr\rvert &= {\rm O} \biggl(\frac{1}{\log^m N} \biggr), \end{align*} as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Combine (3.2)-(3.4) and take sup over $\xi$.

nodes.name: Moment bound for Piatetski-Shapiro exponential sums
nodes.statement: Suppose $b, c \in \mathbb{R}$ and \(k \in \mathbb{N}\), with \(b \geqslant 1\), \(c > 2\), and $2k > (\floor{2c} + 1)(\floor{2c} + 2) + 1$. If $M = \frac{N^{1/c}}{\log^B N}$ for some $B \geqslant 1$, then \[ \sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\!-\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr) \biggr\rvert^{2k} \!\!\! = {\rm O}\bigl(\log^{Bc} N \bigr). \]
nodes.statement_short: The $2k$-th moment over $\xi$ of $|\mathbb{E}_m e(-\xi\lfloor m^c\rfloor/N)|$ is $O(\log^{Bc}N)$.
nodes.label: lem:poulias-bound

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.7
nodes.statement: Suppose $N$ is large (which we will contextualize later). The following holds: \begin{align*} \sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr) \biggr\rvert^{2k} \!\! &\leqslant \sum_{\xi = 1}^{N}\: \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr) \biggr\rvert^{2k}\\ &= \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \biggl(\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr)^k \biggl(\overline{\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)}\biggr)^k\\ \begin{split} &= \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \Biggl(\frac{1}{M^k} \;\cdot\; \smashoperator{\sum_{\mkern30mu m_1, \ldots, m_k \leqslant M}}\quad\, \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} \bigl(\floor{m_1^c} + \cdots + \floor{m_k^c} \bigr)\biggr)\Biggr)\\ &\hphantom{= \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1}}\qquad\: \cdot \Biggl(\frac{1}{M^k} \;\cdot\; \smashoperator{\sum_{\mkern20mu m_{k + 1}, \ldots, m_{2k} \leqslant M}}\quad\;\, \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} \bigl(\floor{m_{k+1}^c} + \cdots + \floor{m_{2k}^c} \bigr)\biggr)\Biggr) \end{split}\\ \begin{split} &= \frac{1}{M^{2k}} \! \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \mkern-25mu \smashoperator[r]{\sum_{\mkern36mu m_1, \ldots, m_{2k} \leqslant M}}\quad\;\, \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} \bigl(\floor{m_1^c} + \cdots + \floor{m_k^c}\\[-1.2em] &\hphantom{= \frac{1}{M^{2k}} \! \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \mkern-25mu \smashoperator[r]{\sum_{\mkern36mu m_1, \ldots, m_{2k} \leqslant M}}\quad\;\, \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} \bigl(\floor{m_1^c}}\: - \floor{m_{k + 1}^c} - \cdots - \floor{m_{2k}^c} \bigr)\biggr). \end{split} \end{align*} Note that, for any $R \in \mathbb{Z}$, \begin{equation*} \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} R \biggr) =\begin{cases} N &\text{if } N \mid R\\ \hfil 0 &\text{if } N \nmid R \end{cases}. \end{equation*} By hypothesis, we take \(N\) sufficiently large to have \begin{align*} \begin{split} \bigl\lvert \floor{m_1^c} + \cdots + \floor{m_k^c} - \floor{m_{k + 1}^c} &- \cdots - \floor{m_{2k}^c} \bigr\rvert\\ &\leqslant \bigl\lvert \floor{m_1^c} - \floor{m_{k + 1}^c} \bigr\rvert + \cdots + \bigl\lvert \floor{m_k^c} - \floor{m_{2k}^c} \bigr\rvert \end{split}\\ &\leqslant k M^c = \frac{kN}{\log^{Bc} N} < N. \end{align*} Therefore, \begin{equation*} \sum_{\xi = 1}^{N} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr) \biggr\rvert^{2k} \!\!\! = \frac{N}{M^{2k}} \cdot G(M), \end{equation*} where $G(M)$ is the number of solutions to the equation \begin{equation} \floor{m_1^c} + \cdots + \floor{m_k^c} - \floor{m_{k + 1}^c} - \cdots - \floor{m_{2k}^c} = 0 \end{equation} inside the $2k$-dimensional cube $\{1, \ldots , M\}^{2k}$. Now, suppose that $(m_1, \ldots, m_{2k})$ satisfies \cref{eqn:2k-dim-cube}. Then, \begin{align} \begin{split}\nonumber \bigl\lvert m_1^c + \cdots + m_k^c - m_{k + 1}^c &- \cdots - m_{2k}^c \bigr\rvert\\ &= \bigl\lvert \{m_1^c\} - \{m_{k + 1}^c\} + \cdots + \{m_k^c\} - \{m_{2k}^c\} \bigr\rvert \end{split}\\ &\leqslant \bigl\lvert \{m_1^c\} - \{m_{k + 1}^c\} \bigr\rvert + \cdots + \bigl\lvert \{m_k^c\} - \{m_{2k}^c\} \bigr\rvert < k. \end{align} Thus, $G(M)$ is less than or equal to the number of solutions of the above inequality. By Poulias (\cref{thm:poulias}), this number is \[ 2k \Omega M^{2k - c} + {\rm o}(M^{2k - c}) = {\rm O}(M^{2k - c}), \] where $\Omega$ is a positive constant. So, $G(M) = {\rm O}(M^{2k - c})$ and \begin{equation*} \sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr) \biggr\rvert^{2k} \!\!\! = {\rm O} \biggl(\frac{N}{M^c} \biggr) = {\rm O}\bigl(\log^{Bc} N \bigr). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand the $2k$-th moment, use orthogonality to count solutions of a floor equation, bound by Poulias's Diophantine inequality count.

nodes.name: Floor Diophantine equation
nodes.statement: \floor{m_1^c} + \cdots + \floor{m_k^c} - \floor{m_{k + 1}^c} - \cdots - \floor{m_{2k}^c} = 0
nodes.label: eqn:2k-dim-cube

nodes.name: Diophantine inequality
nodes.statement: \begin{split}\nonumber \bigl\lvert m_1^c + \cdots + m_k^c - m_{k + 1}^c &- \cdots - m_{2k}^c \bigr\rvert\\ &= \bigl\lvert \{m_1^c\} - \{m_{k + 1}^c\} + \cdots + \{m_k^c\} - \{m_{2k}^c\} \bigr\rvert \end{split}\\ &\leqslant \bigl\lvert \{m_1^c\} - \{m_{k + 1}^c\} \bigr\rvert + \cdots + \bigl\lvert \{m_k^c\} - \{m_{2k}^c\} \bigr\rvert < k.
nodes.label: eqn:diophantine-inequality

nodes.name: Expand the moment
nodes.statement: Suppose $N$ is large (which we will contextualize later). The following holds: \begin{align*} \sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr) \biggr\rvert^{2k} \!\! &\leqslant \sum_{\xi = 1}^{N}\: \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr) \biggr\rvert^{2k}\\ &= \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \biggl(\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr)^k \biggl(\overline{\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)}\biggr)^k\\ \begin{split} &= \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \Biggl(\frac{1}{M^k} \;\cdot\; \smashoperator{\sum_{\mkern30mu m_1, \ldots, m_k \leqslant M}}\quad\, \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} \bigl(\floor{m_1^c} + \cdots + \floor{m_k^c} \bigr)\biggr)\Biggr)\\ &\hphantom{= \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1}}\qquad\: \cdot \Biggl(\frac{1}{M^k} \;\cdot\; \smashoperator{\sum_{\mkern20mu m_{k + 1}, \ldots, m_{2k} \leqslant M}}\quad\;\, \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} \bigl(\floor{m_{k+1}^c} + \cdots + \floor{m_{2k}^c} \bigr)\biggr)\Biggr) \end{split}\\ \begin{split} &= \frac{1}{M^{2k}} \! \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \mkern-25mu \smashoperator[r]{\sum_{\mkern36mu m_1, \ldots, m_{2k} \leqslant M}}\quad\;\, \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} \bigl(\floor{m_1^c} + \cdots + \floor{m_k^c}\\[-1.2em] &\hphantom{= \frac{1}{M^{2k}} \! \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \mkern-25mu \smashoperator[r]{\sum_{\mkern36mu m_1, \ldots, m_{2k} \leqslant M}}\quad\;\, \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} \bigl(\floor{m_1^c}}\: - \floor{m_{k + 1}^c} - \cdots - \floor{m_{2k}^c} \bigr)\biggr). \end{split} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand $|\cdot|^{2k}$ into a $2k$-fold sum.

nodes.name: Orthogonality
nodes.statement: Note that, for any $R \in \mathbb{Z}$, \begin{equation*} \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} R \biggr) =\begin{cases} N &\text{if } N \mid R\\ \hfil 0 &\text{if } N \nmid R \end{cases}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Character sum over $\xi$ is $N$ or 0.

nodes.name: Size of the difference
nodes.statement: By hypothesis, we take \(N\) sufficiently large to have \begin{align*} \begin{split} \bigl\lvert \floor{m_1^c} + \cdots + \floor{m_k^c} - \floor{m_{k + 1}^c} &- \cdots - \floor{m_{2k}^c} \bigr\rvert\\ &\leqslant \bigl\lvert \floor{m_1^c} - \floor{m_{k + 1}^c} \bigr\rvert + \cdots + \bigl\lvert \floor{m_k^c} - \floor{m_{2k}^c} \bigr\rvert \end{split}\\ &\leqslant k M^c = \frac{kN}{\log^{Bc} N} < N. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The floor combination is below $N$ in absolute value.

nodes.name: Count G(M)
nodes.statement: Therefore, \begin{equation*} \sum_{\xi = 1}^{N} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr) \biggr\rvert^{2k} \!\!\! = \frac{N}{M^{2k}} \cdot G(M), \end{equation*} where $G(M)$ is the number of solutions to the equation \begin{equation} \floor{m_1^c} + \cdots + \floor{m_k^c} - \floor{m_{k + 1}^c} - \cdots - \floor{m_{2k}^c} = 0 \end{equation} inside the $2k$-dimensional cube $\{1, \ldots , M\}^{2k}$.
nodes.statement_short: The moment equals $N G(M)/M^{2k}$ with $G(M)$ the solution count of (3.5).

nodes.name: Remove floors
nodes.statement: Now, suppose that $(m_1, \ldots, m_{2k})$ satisfies \cref{eqn:2k-dim-cube}. Then, \begin{align} \begin{split}\nonumber \bigl\lvert m_1^c + \cdots + m_k^c - m_{k + 1}^c &- \cdots - m_{2k}^c \bigr\rvert\\ &= \bigl\lvert \{m_1^c\} - \{m_{k + 1}^c\} + \cdots + \{m_k^c\} - \{m_{2k}^c\} \bigr\rvert \end{split}\\ &\leqslant \bigl\lvert \{m_1^c\} - \{m_{k + 1}^c\} \bigr\rvert + \cdots + \bigl\lvert \{m_k^c\} - \{m_{2k}^c\} \bigr\rvert < k. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Solutions of (3.5) satisfy the inequality (3.6).

nodes.name: Apply Poulias
nodes.statement: Thus, $G(M)$ is less than or equal to the number of solutions of the above inequality. By Poulias (\cref{thm:poulias}), this number is \[ 2k \Omega M^{2k - c} + {\rm o}(M^{2k - c}) = {\rm O}(M^{2k - c}), \] where $\Omega$ is a positive constant. So, $G(M) = {\rm O}(M^{2k - c})$ and \begin{equation*} \sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr) \biggr\rvert^{2k} \!\!\! = {\rm O} \biggl(\frac{N}{M^c} \biggr) = {\rm O}\bigl(\log^{Bc} N \bigr). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Poulias gives $G(M)=O(M^{2k-c})$, hence the bound.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.2
nodes.statement: Suppose $k$ is as in \cref{lem:poulias-bound}. Observe that \begin{align*} \sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2 \!\biggl(\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! &-\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr) \leqslant \sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^{\frac{1}{k}} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^{2 - \frac{1}{k}} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr\rvert\\ &\leqslant\: \sup_{\xi}\; \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^{\frac{1}{k}}\sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^{2 - \frac{1}{k}} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr\rvert\\ &\leqslant\: \sup_{\xi}\; \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^{\frac{1}{k}} \Biggl(\sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert ^2 \Biggr)^{\!\!\! 1 - \frac{1}{2k}} \! \Biggl(\sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr\rvert^{2k} \Biggr)^{\frac{1}{2k}} \end{align*} by H\"{o}lder's inequality. Therefore, by the previous lemmas, \begin{align*} \sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2 \Biggl(\frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^M \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\Biggr) &= \underbrace{{\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^{A + 1 + \frac{Bc}{2k}} N} \biggr)}_{\cref{lem:rational-approx-bound},\ \cref{lem:small-xi-bound}} \underbrace{{\rm O}(\log N)}_{\cref{lem:parseval-bound}} \underbrace{{\rm O}\bigl(\log^{\frac{Bc}{2k}} N \bigr)}_{\cref{lem:poulias-bound}}\\ &= {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^A N}\biggr). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Hölder's inequality decouples the sum; combine Lemmas 3.4-3.7.

nodes.name: Hölder
nodes.statement: Suppose $k$ is as in \cref{lem:poulias-bound}. Observe that \begin{align*} \sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2 \!\biggl(\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! &-\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr) \leqslant \sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^{\frac{1}{k}} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^{2 - \frac{1}{k}} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr\rvert\\ &\leqslant\: \sup_{\xi}\; \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^{\frac{1}{k}}\sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^{2 - \frac{1}{k}} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr\rvert\\ &\leqslant\: \sup_{\xi}\; \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^{\frac{1}{k}} \Biggl(\sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert ^2 \Biggr)^{\!\!\! 1 - \frac{1}{2k}} \! \Biggl(\sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr\rvert^{2k} \Biggr)^{\frac{1}{2k}} \end{align*} by H\"{o}lder's inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Factor out $\sup|\hat\Lambda/N|^{1/k}$ and apply Hölder.

nodes.name: Combine lemmas
nodes.statement: Therefore, by the previous lemmas, \begin{align*} \sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{\log^b N}} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2 \Biggl(\frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^M \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\Biggr) &= \underbrace{{\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^{A + 1 + \frac{Bc}{2k}} N} \biggr)}_{\cref{lem:rational-approx-bound},\ \cref{lem:small-xi-bound}} \underbrace{{\rm O}(\log N)}_{\cref{lem:parseval-bound}} \underbrace{{\rm O}\bigl(\log^{\frac{Bc}{2k}} N \bigr)}_{\cref{lem:poulias-bound}}\\ &= {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^A N}\biggr). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Insert the bounds of Lemmas 3.4-3.7.

nodes.name: Proof idea for Proposition 3.3
nodes.statement: The idea is as follows: We factor out the supremum of the exponential sum, which decouples the product and allows us to use Parseval's identity (\cref{thm:parseval}) on the $\hat{\Lambda}$ term. It then remains to bound $\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}(-\xi \floor{m^c}/N)$ uniformly for $N/\log^b N \leqslant \xi \leqslant N/2$. For this, we first partition the unit interval into intervals \(P\) of equal length, then approximate the sum of interest by a sum involving $\mathrm{e}(-\xi m^c/N)$. After doing so, the approximating sum still includes a term $\textbf{1}_{P}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr)$ that needs to be dealt with. We do this by writing this sum in terms of probability measures and using the Erd\H{o}s-Tur{\'a}n{} inequality (\cref{thm:erdos-turan}). This process reduces the problem into bounding exponential sums of the form $\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}(um^c)$, which we do by van der Corput's method (\cref{thm:vdc-estimate}). For \(c > 12\), Deshouillers has proven better bounds for these sums \cite{deshouillers1973}, but van der Corput's method applies to all $c > 0$, so we prefer to use this method for a unified treatment.
nodes.statement_short: Sketch: factor out the sup of the exponential sum, use Parseval; remove the floor via a partition and Erdős-Turán, then van der Corput.

nodes.name: Factor out and Parseval
nodes.statement: The idea is as follows: We factor out the supremum of the exponential sum, which decouples the product and allows us to use Parseval's identity (\cref{thm:parseval}) on the $\hat{\Lambda}$ term. It then remains to bound $\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}(-\xi \floor{m^c}/N)$ uniformly for $N/\log^b N \leqslant \xi \leqslant N/2$.
nodes.statement_short: Factor out the sup; Parseval handles $\hat\Lambda$; remains a uniform exponential sum bound.

nodes.name: Partition approximation
nodes.statement: For this, we first partition the unit interval into intervals \(P\) of equal length, then approximate the sum of interest by a sum involving $\mathrm{e}(-\xi m^c/N)$. After doing so, the approximating sum still includes a term $\textbf{1}_{P}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr)$ that needs to be dealt with.
nodes.statement_short: Partition the circle and approximate by sums of $e(-\xi m^c/N)$.

nodes.name: Erdős-Turán
nodes.statement: We do this by writing this sum in terms of probability measures and using the Erd\H{o}s-Tur{\'a}n{} inequality (\cref{thm:erdos-turan}).
nodes.statement_short: Handle the indicator via measures and Erdős-Turán.

nodes.name: van der Corput
nodes.statement: This process reduces the problem into bounding exponential sums of the form $\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}(um^c)$, which we do by van der Corput's method (\cref{thm:vdc-estimate}). For \(c > 12\), Deshouillers has proven better bounds for these sums \cite{deshouillers1973}, but van der Corput's method applies to all $c > 0$, so we prefer to use this method for a unified treatment.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\mathbb{E}_m e(um^c)$ by van der Corput.

nodes.name: Partition bound for the exponential sum
nodes.statement: Let \(\textbf{P}\) be a partition of \(S^1\) into intervals \(P\) of equal length \(\gamma\). Then, \[ \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} \floor{m^c} \!\biggr) \biggr\rvert \leqslant \sum_{P \in \textbf{P}}\: \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{P}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \biggr\rvert + 4\pi\frac{\xi}{N} \gamma. \]
assumptions: Let \(\textbf{P}\) be a partition of \(S^1\) into intervals \(P\) of equal length \(\gamma\).
nodes.statement_short: Replace $\lfloor m^c\rfloor$ by $m^c$ at cost $4\pi\gamma\xi/N$, summing over a partition into arcs of length $\gamma$.
nodes.label: lem:partition-bound

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.8
nodes.statement: Let \(\textbf{P}\) be a partition of \(S^1\) into intervals \([a_i, b_i)\) of length \(\gamma\). Then, \begin{equation} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} \{m^c\} \!\biggr) \biggr\rvert = \biggl\lvert \sum_{[a_i, b_i) \in \textbf{P}} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} \{m^c\} \!\biggr) \biggr\rvert. \end{equation} Now, since summands in the above expression are nonzero only when \(\{m_c\} \in [a_i, b_i)\), by the triangle inequality we have \begin{align} \begin{split}\nonumber \eqref{eqn:partition-setup} &\leqslant \biggl\lvert \sum_{[a_i, b_i) \in \textbf{P}} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \underbrace{\mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} a_i \biggr)}_{\leqslant 1} \biggr\rvert + \sum_{[a_i, b_i) \in \textbf{P}} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \biggl\lvert \underbrace{\mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c\biggr)}_{\leqslant 1}\biggr\rvert\\[-0.7em] &\qquad\qquad\qquad\; \cdot\; \biggl\lvert \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} \{m^c\} \!\biggr) - \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} a_i \biggr) \biggr\rvert \end{split}\\[.2em] \begin{split}\nonumber &\leqslant \sum_{[a_i, b_i) \in \textbf{P}}\, \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \biggr\rvert\\[-0.7em] &\qquad\qquad\qquad + \underbrace{\biggl(\sum_{[a_i, b_i) \in \textbf{P}} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \biggr)}_{\leqslant 1} \Biggl(\sup_{\substack{\lvert y - x \rvert \leqslant \gamma \\ 0 \leqslant x, y \leqslant 1}} \biggl\lvert \, \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} y \!\biggr) - \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} x \!\biggr) \biggr\rvert \Biggr) \end{split}\\ &\leqslant \sum_{[a_i, b_i) \in \textbf{P}}\, \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \biggr\rvert + 4\pi\frac{\xi}{N} \gamma. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Split by partition arcs, replace $\{m^c\}$ by the arc's left end, and bound the error by the triangle inequality.

nodes.name: Partition decomposition
nodes.statement: \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} \{m^c\} \!\biggr) \biggr\rvert = \biggl\lvert \sum_{[a_i, b_i) \in \textbf{P}} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} \{m^c\} \!\biggr) \biggr\rvert.
nodes.label: eqn:partition-setup

nodes.name: Partition sum bound
nodes.statement: \begin{split}\nonumber \eqref{eqn:partition-setup} &\leqslant \biggl\lvert \sum_{[a_i, b_i) \in \textbf{P}} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \underbrace{\mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} a_i \biggr)}_{\leqslant 1} \biggr\rvert + \sum_{[a_i, b_i) \in \textbf{P}} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \biggl\lvert \underbrace{\mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c\biggr)}_{\leqslant 1}\biggr\rvert\\[-0.7em] &\qquad\qquad\qquad\; \cdot\; \biggl\lvert \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} \{m^c\} \!\biggr) - \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} a_i \biggr) \biggr\rvert \end{split}\\[.2em] \begin{split}\nonumber &\leqslant \sum_{[a_i, b_i) \in \textbf{P}}\, \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \biggr\rvert\\[-0.7em] &\qquad\qquad\qquad + \underbrace{\biggl(\sum_{[a_i, b_i) \in \textbf{P}} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \biggr)}_{\leqslant 1} \Biggl(\sup_{\substack{\lvert y - x \rvert \leqslant \gamma \\ 0 \leqslant x, y \leqslant 1}} \biggl\lvert \, \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} y \!\biggr) - \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} x \!\biggr) \biggr\rvert \Biggr) \end{split}\\ &\leqslant \sum_{[a_i, b_i) \in \textbf{P}}\, \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \biggr\rvert + 4\pi\frac{\xi}{N} \gamma.
nodes.label: eqn:partition-sum

nodes.name: Partition
nodes.statement: Let \(\textbf{P}\) be a partition of \(S^1\) into intervals \([a_i, b_i)\) of length \(\gamma\). Then, \begin{equation} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} \{m^c\} \!\biggr) \biggr\rvert = \biggl\lvert \sum_{[a_i, b_i) \in \textbf{P}} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} \{m^c\} \!\biggr) \biggr\rvert. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Decompose the sum over the arcs of the partition.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality
nodes.statement: Now, since summands in the above expression are nonzero only when \(\{m_c\} \in [a_i, b_i)\), by the triangle inequality we have \begin{align} \begin{split}\nonumber \eqref{eqn:partition-setup} &\leqslant \biggl\lvert \sum_{[a_i, b_i) \in \textbf{P}} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \underbrace{\mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} a_i \biggr)}_{\leqslant 1} \biggr\rvert + \sum_{[a_i, b_i) \in \textbf{P}} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \biggl\lvert \underbrace{\mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c\biggr)}_{\leqslant 1}\biggr\rvert\\[-0.7em] &\qquad\qquad\qquad\; \cdot\; \biggl\lvert \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} \{m^c\} \!\biggr) - \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} a_i \biggr) \biggr\rvert \end{split}\\[.2em] \begin{split}\nonumber &\leqslant \sum_{[a_i, b_i) \in \textbf{P}}\, \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \biggr\rvert\\[-0.7em] &\qquad\qquad\qquad + \underbrace{\biggl(\sum_{[a_i, b_i) \in \textbf{P}} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \biggr)}_{\leqslant 1} \Biggl(\sup_{\substack{\lvert y - x \rvert \leqslant \gamma \\ 0 \leqslant x, y \leqslant 1}} \biggl\lvert \, \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} y \!\biggr) - \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi}{N} x \!\biggr) \biggr\rvert \Biggr) \end{split}\\ &\leqslant \sum_{[a_i, b_i) \in \textbf{P}}\, \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{[a_i, b_i)}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \biggr\rvert + 4\pi\frac{\xi}{N} \gamma. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Freeze $\{m^c\}$ at each arc's endpoint; the error is at most $4\pi\gamma\xi/N$.

nodes.name: Measure decomposition bound
nodes.statement: Define the measures \begin{align*} &\mu = \!\! \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \delta_{\{m^c\}},\\ &\mu_1 = \frac{1}{1 + c_1}\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m\leqslant M} \biggl(1 + \cos\biggl(\! -\frac{2 \pi i \xi m^c}{N} \biggr) \biggr)\delta_{\{m^c\}},\\ &\mu_2 = \frac{1}{1 + c_2}\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M}\biggl(1 + \sin\biggl(\! -\frac{2 \pi i \xi m^c}{N}\biggr)\biggr)\delta_{\{m^c\}}, \text{ and } \\ &\mu_3 = \!\! \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \delta_{\{m^c\}}, \end{align*} where \begin{equation*} c_1 = \!\! \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \cos\biggl(\! -\frac{2\pi i \xi m^c}{N} \biggr) \text{ and } c_2 = \!\! \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \sin\biggl(\! -\frac{2\pi i \xi m^c}{N}\biggr). \end{equation*} Then \begin{equation*} \lvert \mu(P) \rvert \leqslant 5 \Bigl(\bigl\lvert \mu_1(P) - \mathrm{Leb}(P) \bigr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \mu_2(P) - \mathrm{Leb}(P) \bigr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \delta_{\{m^c\}}(P) - \mathrm{Leb}(P) \bigr\rvert \Bigr). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Define $\mu,\mu_1,\mu_2,\mu_3$; then $|\mu(P)|$ is bounded by the discrepancies of $\mu_1,\mu_2,\mu_3$ from Lebesgue measure.
nodes.label: lem:measure-stuff

nodes.name: mu_1 and mu_2 are probability measures
nodes.statement: Note that $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ are probability measures on the unit circle.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.9
nodes.statement: Observe that \[ \mu = (1 + c_1)\mu_1 + i(1 + c_2)\mu_2 - \bigl((1 + c_1)\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \delta_{\{m^c\}} + i(1 + c_2)\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M}\delta_{\{m^c\}}\bigr). \] By the triangle inequality, \[ \lvert \mu \rvert \leqslant (1 + c_1) \bigl(\lvert \mu_1 - \mathrm{Leb}\rvert + \lvert\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M}\delta_{\{m^c\}} - \mathrm{Leb} \rvert \bigr) + (1 + c_2) \bigl(\lvert \mu_2 - \mathrm{Leb} \rvert + \lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M}\delta_{\{m^c\}} - \mathrm{Leb} \rvert \bigr). \] Noting that $c_1, c_2 \leqslant 1$, we conclude.
nodes.statement_short: Write $\mu$ as a combination of $\mu_1,\mu_2,\mu_3$ and use the triangle inequality.

nodes.name: Decompose mu
nodes.statement: Observe that \[ \mu = (1 + c_1)\mu_1 + i(1 + c_2)\mu_2 - \bigl((1 + c_1)\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \delta_{\{m^c\}} + i(1 + c_2)\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M}\delta_{\{m^c\}}\bigr). \]
nodes.statement_short: Express $\mu$ via $\mu_1,\mu_2,\mu_3$.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality
nodes.statement: By the triangle inequality, \[ \lvert \mu \rvert \leqslant (1 + c_1) \bigl(\lvert \mu_1 - \mathrm{Leb}\rvert + \lvert\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M}\delta_{\{m^c\}} - \mathrm{Leb} \rvert \bigr) + (1 + c_2) \bigl(\lvert \mu_2 - \mathrm{Leb} \rvert + \lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M}\delta_{\{m^c\}} - \mathrm{Leb} \rvert \bigr). \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound $|\mu|$ by discrepancies.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Noting that $c_1, c_2 \leqslant 1$, we conclude.
nodes.statement_short: Use $c_1,c_2\le1$.

nodes.name: Fourier coefficients of mu_1, mu_2, mu_3
nodes.statement: For $k \geqslant 1$, in view of the trivial identity $\bigl\{k\{m^c\}\bigr\} = \{km^c\}$, \begin{align*} \hat{\mu}_1(k) &= \frac{1}{1 + c_1} \biggl(\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M}\mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{k m^c}{N} \biggr) + \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{k m^c}{N} \biggr) \cos\biggl(\! -\frac{2\pi i \xi m^c}{N} \biggr) \biggr),\\ \hat{\mu}_2(k) &= \frac{1}{1 + c_2} \biggl(\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{km^c}{N} \biggr) + \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{km^c}{N} \biggr) \sin\biggl(\! -\frac{2\pi i \xi m^c}{N} \biggr) \biggr), \text{ and}\\ \hat{\mu}_3(k) &= \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{km^c}{N} \biggr). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Explicit formulas for $\hat\mu_1(k),\hat\mu_2(k),\hat\mu_3(k)$ as averages of exponentials in $m^c$.

nodes.name: Fourier coefficient bounds for the measures
nodes.statement: For $k \geqslant 1$, \begin{equation*} \bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_1(k) \bigr\rvert, \bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_2(k) \bigr\rvert \leqslant 2\Biggl(\biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\Bigl(k - \frac{\xi}{N} \Bigr) m^c \biggr) \biggr\rvert + \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\Bigl(k + \frac{\xi}{N} \Bigr)m^c \Bigr) \biggr)\biggr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_3(k) \bigr\rvert \Biggr). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: $|\hat\mu_1(k)|,|\hat\mu_2(k)|$ are bounded by exponential sums at frequencies $k\pm\xi/N$ plus $|\hat\mu_3(k)|$.
nodes.label: lem:ft-bounds-for-measures

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.10
nodes.statement: By trigonometric identities and noting that $\lvert c_1 \rvert, \lvert c_2 \rvert \leqslant 1/2$ (in fact, these can be shown to go to zero as $M \to \infty$ by using a van der Corput argument similar to \cref{prop:estimate-sigma2-details}), \begin{align*} \bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_1(k) \bigr\rvert &= \frac{1}{1 + c_1} \biggl\lvert\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \bigl(\cos(2\pi km^c) + i \sin(2\pi k m^c)\bigr) \cos\biggl(\!-\frac{2\pi i \xi m^c}{N}\biggr) + \hat{\mu}_3(k) \biggr\rvert \\ \begin{split} &\leqslant 2\Biggl(\Biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \cos\biggl(2\pi \Bigl(k - \frac{\xi}{N} \Bigr) m^c \biggr) + \cos\biggl(2\pi \Bigl(k + \frac{\xi}{N}\Bigr) m^c \biggr)\\ &\qquad\qquad + i\Biggl(\sin\biggl(2\pi \Bigl(k + \frac{\xi}{N}\Bigr) m^c \biggr) + \sin\biggl(2\pi \Bigl(k - \frac{\xi}{N}\Bigr) m^c \biggr)\Biggr) \Biggr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_3(k) \bigr\rvert \Biggr) \end{split}\\ &\leqslant 2\Biggl(\biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\Bigl(k - \frac{\xi}{N}\Bigr) m^c \biggr)\biggr\rvert + \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\Bigl(k + \frac{\xi}{N}\Bigr) m^c \biggr)\biggr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_3(k) \bigr\rvert \Biggr). \end{align*} Similarly, \begin{align*} \bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_2(k) \bigr\rvert &= \frac{1}{1 + c_2} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \bigl(\cos(2\pi km^c) + i \sin(2\pi k m^c) \bigr) \sin\biggl(\! -\frac{2\pi i \xi m^c}{N} \biggr) + \hat{\mu}_3(k) \biggr\rvert\\ \begin{split} &\leqslant 2\Biggl(\Biggl\lvert\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \sin\biggl(2\pi \Bigl(k - \frac{\xi}{N} \Bigr)m^c \biggr) - \sin\biggr(2\pi \Bigl(k + \frac{\xi}{N} \Bigr)m^c \biggr)\\ &\qquad\qquad + i \Biggl(\cos\biggl(2\pi \Bigl(k + \frac{\xi}{N} \Bigr) m^c \biggr) - \cos\biggl(2\pi \Bigl(k - \frac{\xi}{N} \Bigr)m^c \biggr)\Biggr) \Biggr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_3(k) \bigr\rvert \Biggr) \end{split}\\ &\leqslant 2 \Biggl(\biggl\lvert\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\Bigl(k - \frac{\xi}{N} \Bigr) m^c \biggr) \biggr\rvert + \biggl\lvert\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\Bigl(k + \frac{\xi}{N}\Bigr)m^c \biggr) \biggr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_3(k) \bigr\rvert \Biggr). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Trigonometric product-to-sum identities with $|c_1|,|c_2|\le1/2$.

nodes.name: Exponential sum on an arc as a measure
nodes.statement: Let $\mu$ be defined as in \cref{lem:measure-stuff}. Then, \begin{equation} \begin{split} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} &\textbf{1}_{P}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \biggr\rvert\\ &\leqslant 5\Bigl(\bigl\lvert \mu_1(P) - \mathrm{Leb}(P) \bigr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \mu_2(P) - \mathrm{Leb}(P) \bigr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \delta_{\{m^c\}}(P) - \mathrm{Leb}(P) \bigr\rvert \Bigr). \end{split} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $|\mathbb{E}_m 1_P(\{m^c\})e(-\xi m^c/N)|$ is bounded by the discrepancies of $\mu_1,\mu_2,\mu_3$ on $P$.
nodes.label: lem:expectation-to-measure

nodes.name: Arc sum bound via measures
nodes.statement: \begin{split} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} &\textbf{1}_{P}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \biggr\rvert\\ &\leqslant 5\Bigl(\bigl\lvert \mu_1(P) - \mathrm{Leb}(P) \bigr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \mu_2(P) - \mathrm{Leb}(P) \bigr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \delta_{\{m^c\}}(P) - \mathrm{Leb}(P) \bigr\rvert \Bigr). \end{split}
nodes.label: eqn:turan-prep

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.11
nodes.statement: Noticing that \begin{equation*} \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{P}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \biggr\rvert = \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \delta_{\{m^c\}}(P) \biggr\rvert = \bigl\lvert \mu(P) \bigr\rvert, \end{equation*} the result is immediate from \cref{lem:measure-stuff}.
nodes.statement_short: The arc sum equals $|\mu(P)|$; apply Lemma 3.9.

nodes.name: Erdős-Turán bound for the exponential sum
nodes.statement: Let $K \in \mathbb{Z}^{+}$ be arbitrary. Then \begin{equation} \begin{split} \sup_{\mkern-10mu \frac{N}{\log^b{N}} \leqslant \xi < \frac{N}{2}} &\biggl\lvert\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi\floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr) \biggr\rvert\\ &\qquad \leqslant \;\;\smashoperator[l]{\sup_{\mkern-10mu \frac{N}{\log^b{N}} \leqslant \xi < \frac{N}{2}}} \Biggl\lvert \frac{100}{\gamma} \biggl(\frac{1}{K} + \sum_{k = 1}^{K} \frac{\bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_1(k) \bigr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_2(k) \bigr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_3(k) \bigr\rvert}{k} \biggr) + 4\pi\frac{\xi}{N} \gamma \Biggr\rvert. \end{split} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The sup over far $\xi$ of the floor exponential sum is bounded by $\gamma^{-1}$ times Erdős-Turán terms in $\hat\mu_i$ plus $4\pi\gamma\xi/N$.
nodes.label: lem:turan-bound

nodes.name: Erdős-Turán bound for exponential sum
nodes.statement: \begin{split} \sup_{\mkern-10mu \frac{N}{\log^b{N}} \leqslant \xi < \frac{N}{2}} &\biggl\lvert\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi\floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr) \biggr\rvert\\ &\qquad \leqslant \;\;\smashoperator[l]{\sup_{\mkern-10mu \frac{N}{\log^b{N}} \leqslant \xi < \frac{N}{2}}} \Biggl\lvert \frac{100}{\gamma} \biggl(\frac{1}{K} + \sum_{k = 1}^{K} \frac{\bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_1(k) \bigr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_2(k) \bigr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_3(k) \bigr\rvert}{k} \biggr) + 4\pi\frac{\xi}{N} \gamma \Biggr\rvert. \end{split}
nodes.label: eqn:exp-sum

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.12
nodes.statement: Fix some $\xi$ satisfying $N/\log^b{N} \leqslant \xi < N/2$.
