In order of application, by \cref{lem:partition-bound}, by \cref{lem:expectation-to-measure}, by the fact that $\lvert \textbf{P}\rvert = 1/\gamma$, by the Erd\H{o}s-Tur{\'a}n{} inequality (\cref{thm:erdos-turan}), and by the triangle inequality, \begin{align*} \biggl\lvert\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi\floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr) \biggr\rvert &\leqslant \sum_{P \in \textbf{P}}\: \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{P}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \biggr\rvert + 4\pi\frac{\xi}{N} \gamma\\ \begin{split} &\leqslant 5\sum_{P \in \textbf{P}} \Bigl(\bigl\lvert \mu_1(P) - \mathrm{Leb}(P)\bigr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \mu_2(P) - \mathrm{Leb}(P) \bigr\rvert\\[-1.2em] &\hphantom{\leqslant 5\sum_{P \in \textbf{P}} \Bigl(\bigl\lvert\mu_1(P) - \mathrm{Leb}(P)\bigr\rvert}\; + \bigl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \delta_{\{m^c\}}(P) - \mathrm{Leb}(P) \bigr\rvert \Bigr) + 4\pi\frac{\xi}{N}\gamma \end{split}\\ &\leqslant \frac{50}{\gamma}\biggl(\frac{1}{K} + \sum_{k = 1}^{K} \frac{\bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_1(k) \bigr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_2(k) \bigr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_3(k) \bigr\rvert}{k} \biggr) + 4\pi\frac{\xi}{N} \gamma. \end{align*} Then \cref{eqn:exp-sum} follows by taking suprema.
nodes.statement_short: Chain Lemma 3.8, Lemma 3.11, $|\mathbf{P}|=1/\gamma$, Erdős-Turán and the triangle inequality; take suprema.

nodes.name: Chain of bounds
nodes.statement: Fix some $\xi$ satisfying $N/\log^b{N} \leqslant \xi < N/2$. In order of application, by \cref{lem:partition-bound}, by \cref{lem:expectation-to-measure}, by the fact that $\lvert \textbf{P}\rvert = 1/\gamma$, by the Erd\H{o}s-Tur{\'a}n{} inequality (\cref{thm:erdos-turan}), and by the triangle inequality, \begin{align*} \biggl\lvert\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\frac{\xi\floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr) \biggr\rvert &\leqslant \sum_{P \in \textbf{P}}\: \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \textbf{1}_{P}\bigl(\{m^c\}\bigr) \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} m^c \biggr) \biggr\rvert + 4\pi\frac{\xi}{N} \gamma\\ \begin{split} &\leqslant 5\sum_{P \in \textbf{P}} \Bigl(\bigl\lvert \mu_1(P) - \mathrm{Leb}(P)\bigr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \mu_2(P) - \mathrm{Leb}(P) \bigr\rvert\\[-1.2em] &\hphantom{\leqslant 5\sum_{P \in \textbf{P}} \Bigl(\bigl\lvert\mu_1(P) - \mathrm{Leb}(P)\bigr\rvert}\; + \bigl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \delta_{\{m^c\}}(P) - \mathrm{Leb}(P) \bigr\rvert \Bigr) + 4\pi\frac{\xi}{N}\gamma \end{split}\\ &\leqslant \frac{50}{\gamma}\biggl(\frac{1}{K} + \sum_{k = 1}^{K} \frac{\bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_1(k) \bigr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_2(k) \bigr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \hat{\mu}_3(k) \bigr\rvert}{k} \biggr) + 4\pi\frac{\xi}{N} \gamma. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: For fixed $\xi$ apply the partition, measure and Erdős-Turán bounds in turn.

nodes.name: Take suprema
nodes.statement: Then \cref{eqn:exp-sum} follows by taking suprema.
nodes.statement_short: Take sup over $\xi$.

nodes.name: Bound on the sum of the measures' Fourier coefficients
nodes.statement: First, note that the sum of absolute values of $\hat{\mu}_i$ is at most \begin{equation*} 10 \Biggl( \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl( \Bigl(k - \frac{\xi}{N} \Bigr) m^c \biggr) \biggr\rvert + \biggl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl( \Bigl(k + \frac{\xi}{N} \Bigr) m^c \biggr) \biggr\rvert + \bigl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}(km^c) \bigr\rvert \Biggr), \end{equation*} in view of the bounds for the Fourier transforms we proved.
nodes.statement_short: $\sum_i|\hat\mu_i(k)|\le 10$ times three exponential sums at frequencies $k-\xi/N$, $k+\xi/N$, $k$.

nodes.name: Bound in terms of U(xi)
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma = \frac{1}{\log^{A + 1} N}$ and \[ U(\xi) = \frac{1}{K} + \sum_{k = 1}^{K} \frac{\Bigl\lvert \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\Bigl(\bigl(-\frac{\xi}{N} + k\bigr) m^c \Bigr) \Bigr\rvert}{k}. \] Then, \begin{align*} \eqref{eqn:exp-sum}\; &\lesssim \;\,\smashoperator{\sup_{\mkern-10mu \frac{N}{\log^b N} \leqslant \xi < \frac{N}{2}}}\;\; \frac{U(\xi)}{\gamma} + \frac{\xi}{N} \gamma\\ &\leqslant \;\,\smashoperator{\sup_{\mkern-10mu \frac{N}{\log^b{N}} \leqslant \xi < \frac{N}{2}}}\;\; U(\xi) \log^{A+1} N + \frac{1}{\log^{A + 1} N}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: With $\gamma=\log^{-A-1}N$, the bound (3.10) is $\lesssim\sup_\xi U(\xi)\log^{A+1}N+\log^{-A-1}N$.
nodes.label: cor:bound-for-turan-bound

nodes.name: Uniform bound on the far-range exponential sum
nodes.statement: We have \[ \sup_{\mkern-10mu \frac{N}{\log^b N} \leqslant \xi \leqslant \frac{N}{2}} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{M} \sum_{m=1}^M \mathrm{e}\biggl(\!-\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr\rvert = {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^{A+1} N}\biggr). \]
nodes.statement_short: Uniformly for $N/\log^bN\le\xi\le N/2$, $|\mathbb{E}_m e(-\xi\lfloor m^c\rfloor/N)|=O(\log^{-A-1}N)$.
nodes.label: prop:estimate-sigma2-details

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.14
nodes.statement: For each $j \in \mathbb{N}$, let $S_j = [2^{j}, 2^{j + 1}) \cap [1, M]$. Then \begin{equation} \sum_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\Bigl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} + k \Bigr) m^c \biggr) = \sum_j \sum_{m \in S_j} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\Bigl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} + k \Bigr) m^c \biggr). \end{equation} For fixed $k$ and $\xi$, the inner sum is amenable to the van der Corput estimate \cref{thm:vdc-estimate}. Choose $X = 2^j$ and $q = \ceil{c - 2}$. Then \cref{eqn:derv-bound} is satisfied with $B_i$ depending only on $c$, and $F = (-\xi/N + k) X^c \approx kX^c$ . For the terms involving $\mathrm{e}(km^c)$ and $\mathrm{e}\bigl((k + \xi/N) m^c\bigr)$, the proof is identical, since $kX^c \approx (k + \xi/N) X^c$. Since \(X/F \lesssim 1\), we obtain \begin{equation*} \sum_{m \in S_j} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\Bigl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} + k \Bigr) m^c \biggr) \lesssim k^\frac{1}{2^{q + 2} -2 } 2^{j \bigl(1 + \frac{c - q - 2}{2^{q + 2} - 2} \bigr)}. \end{equation*} Summing over $j$ up to $\floor*{\log_2 M}$ and noting that $j = 2^{j + 1} \approx M$, the upper limit, we obtain \begin{equation*} \eqref{eqn:dyadic-sum} \lesssim k^{\frac{1}{2^{q + 2} - 2}} M^{1 + \frac{c - q - 2}{2^{q + 2} - 2}}. \end{equation*} Thus, \begin{align*} U(\xi) &\lesssim \frac{1}{K} + M^{\frac{c - q - 2}{2^{q + 2} - 2}} \sum_{k \leqslant K} k^{\frac{1}{2^{q + 2} - 2} - 1}\\ &\lesssim \frac{1}{K} + M^{\frac{c - q - 2}{2^{q + 2} - 2}}K^{\frac{1}{2^{q + 2} - 2}}. \end{align*} Choosing $K$ so that the two summands above are equal, we see that $U(\xi) \lesssim M^\frac{c - q - 2}{2^{q + 2} - 1}$, independent of $\xi$.
nodes.statement_short: Dyadic decomposition and the van der Corput estimate on each block; optimize $K$ to get $U(\xi)\lesssim M^{-t}$.

nodes.name: Dyadic decomposition
nodes.statement: \sum_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\Bigl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} + k \Bigr) m^c \biggr) = \sum_j \sum_{m \in S_j} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\Bigl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} + k \Bigr) m^c \biggr).
nodes.label: eqn:dyadic-sum

nodes.name: Dyadic split
nodes.statement: For each $j \in \mathbb{N}$, let $S_j = [2^{j}, 2^{j + 1}) \cap [1, M]$. Then \begin{equation} \sum_{m \leqslant M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\Bigl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} + k \Bigr) m^c \biggr) = \sum_j \sum_{m \in S_j} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\Bigl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} + k \Bigr) m^c \biggr). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Split $m\le M$ into dyadic blocks $S_j$.

nodes.name: van der Corput on blocks
nodes.statement: For fixed $k$ and $\xi$, the inner sum is amenable to the van der Corput estimate \cref{thm:vdc-estimate}. Choose $X = 2^j$ and $q = \ceil{c - 2}$. Then \cref{eqn:derv-bound} is satisfied with $B_i$ depending only on $c$, and $F = (-\xi/N + k) X^c \approx kX^c$ . For the terms involving $\mathrm{e}(km^c)$ and $\mathrm{e}\bigl((k + \xi/N) m^c\bigr)$, the proof is identical, since $kX^c \approx (k + \xi/N) X^c$. Since \(X/F \lesssim 1\), we obtain \begin{equation*} \sum_{m \in S_j} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\Bigl(\! -\frac{\xi}{N} + k \Bigr) m^c \biggr) \lesssim k^\frac{1}{2^{q + 2} -2 } 2^{j \bigl(1 + \frac{c - q - 2}{2^{q + 2} - 2} \bigr)}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply Graham-Kolesnik with $X=2^j$, $q=\lceil c-2\rceil$, $F\approx kX^c$.

nodes.name: Sum over blocks
nodes.statement: Summing over $j$ up to $\floor*{\log_2 M}$ and noting that $j = 2^{j + 1} \approx M$, the upper limit, we obtain \begin{equation*} \eqref{eqn:dyadic-sum} \lesssim k^{\frac{1}{2^{q + 2} - 2}} M^{1 + \frac{c - q - 2}{2^{q + 2} - 2}}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Summing the dyadic bounds gives a bound for (3.11).

nodes.name: Optimize K
nodes.statement: Thus, \begin{align*} U(\xi) &\lesssim \frac{1}{K} + M^{\frac{c - q - 2}{2^{q + 2} - 2}} \sum_{k \leqslant K} k^{\frac{1}{2^{q + 2} - 2} - 1}\\ &\lesssim \frac{1}{K} + M^{\frac{c - q - 2}{2^{q + 2} - 2}}K^{\frac{1}{2^{q + 2} - 2}}. \end{align*} Choosing $K$ so that the two summands above are equal, we see that $U(\xi) \lesssim M^\frac{c - q - 2}{2^{q + 2} - 1}$, independent of $\xi$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $U(\xi)$ and choose $K$ to balance terms.

nodes.name: Proposition 3.14 implies Proposition 3.3
nodes.statement: \cref{prop:estimate-sigma2-details} implies \cref{prop:estimate-sigma2}.
nodes.label: lem:sigma2-proof-works

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.15
nodes.statement: Indeed, by \cref{prop:estimate-sigma2-details} we obtain \begin{equation*} \sup_{\mkern-10mu \frac{N}{\log^b N} \leqslant \xi \leqslant \frac{N}{2}} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{M} \sum_{m=1}^M \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr\rvert = {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^{A+1} N}\biggr). \end{equation*} Therefore, \begin{align*} \Biggl\lvert \sum_{\xi = \frac{N}{\log^b N}}^{\frac{N}{2}} \!\biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2 \! \Biggl(\frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^M \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\Biggr)\Biggr\rvert &\leqslant \;\,\smashoperator[l]{\sup_{\mkern-11mu \frac{N}{\log^b N} \leqslant \xi \leqslant \frac{N}{2}}} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^{M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr\rvert \cdot \sum_{\mathclap{r = \frac{N}{\log^b N}}}^{\frac{N}{2}}\: \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(r)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2\\ &\leqslant \;\,\smashoperator[l]{\sup_{\mkern-11mu \frac{N}{\log^b N} \leqslant \xi \leqslant \frac{N}{2}}} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^{M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr\rvert \cdot \sum_{r = 0}^{N - 1}\: \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(r)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2\\ &= \;\,\smashoperator[l]{\sup_{\mkern-11mu \frac{N}{\log^b N} \leqslant \xi \leqslant \frac{N}{2}}} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^{M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr\rvert \cdot\frac{1}{N} \sum_{r = 0}^{N - 1} \bigl(\Lambda(r) \bigr)^2, \end{align*} where the last equality holds due to Parseval's identity (\cref{thm:parseval}). Now, since \begin{equation*} \frac{1}{N} \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \bigl(\Lambda(\xi)\bigr)^2 \leqslant \frac{1}{N} \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(\xi) \cdot \log N, \end{equation*} we have by the Prime Number Theorem that $\frac{1}{N} \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \bigl(\Lambda(\xi) \bigr)^2 = {\rm O}(\log N)$. Therefore, \begin{align*} \sup_{\mkern-10mu \frac{N}{\log^b N} \leqslant \xi \leqslant \frac{N}{2}} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^{M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr\rvert \cdot \frac{1}{N}\sum_{r = 0}^{N - 1} \bigl(\Lambda(r)\bigr)^2 &= {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^{A + 1} N} \biggr) {\rm O}(\log N)\\ &= {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^A N} \biggr), \end{align*} as required. Combining the above with \cref{prop:estimate-sigma1}, we have \begin{equation*} \sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{2}} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2 \Biggl(\frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^M \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\Biggr) = {\rm O} \biggl(\frac{1}{\log^A N}\biggr), \end{equation*} and thus, by symmetry, \begin{equation*} \sum_{\xi = 1}^{N-1} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2 \Biggl(\frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^M \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\Biggr) = {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^A N}\biggr). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Factor out the sup bound of Proposition 3.14 and bound $\sum|\hat\Lambda/N|^2$ by Parseval and the PNT.

nodes.name: Apply Proposition 3.14
nodes.statement: Indeed, by \cref{prop:estimate-sigma2-details} we obtain \begin{equation*} \sup_{\mkern-10mu \frac{N}{\log^b N} \leqslant \xi \leqslant \frac{N}{2}} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{M} \sum_{m=1}^M \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr\rvert = {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^{A+1} N}\biggr). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Uniform bound on the exponential sum.

nodes.name: Factor out and Parseval
nodes.statement: Therefore, \begin{align*} \Biggl\lvert \sum_{\xi = \frac{N}{\log^b N}}^{\frac{N}{2}} \!\biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2 \! \Biggl(\frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^M \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\Biggr)\Biggr\rvert &\leqslant \;\,\smashoperator[l]{\sup_{\mkern-11mu \frac{N}{\log^b N} \leqslant \xi \leqslant \frac{N}{2}}} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^{M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr\rvert \cdot \sum_{\mathclap{r = \frac{N}{\log^b N}}}^{\frac{N}{2}}\: \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(r)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2\\ &\leqslant \;\,\smashoperator[l]{\sup_{\mkern-11mu \frac{N}{\log^b N} \leqslant \xi \leqslant \frac{N}{2}}} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^{M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr\rvert \cdot \sum_{r = 0}^{N - 1}\: \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(r)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2\\ &= \;\,\smashoperator[l]{\sup_{\mkern-11mu \frac{N}{\log^b N} \leqslant \xi \leqslant \frac{N}{2}}} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^{M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr\rvert \cdot\frac{1}{N} \sum_{r = 0}^{N - 1} \bigl(\Lambda(r) \bigr)^2, \end{align*} where the last equality holds due to Parseval's identity (\cref{thm:parseval}).
nodes.statement_short: Pull out the sup and apply Parseval.

nodes.name: PNT bound
nodes.statement: Now, since \begin{equation*} \frac{1}{N} \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \bigl(\Lambda(\xi)\bigr)^2 \leqslant \frac{1}{N} \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \Lambda(\xi) \cdot \log N, \end{equation*} we have by the Prime Number Theorem that $\frac{1}{N} \sum_{\xi = 0}^{N - 1} \bigl(\Lambda(\xi) \bigr)^2 = {\rm O}(\log N)$.
nodes.statement_short: $N^{-1}\sum\Lambda^2=O(\log N)$ by PNT.

nodes.name: Sigma_2 bound
nodes.statement: Therefore, \begin{align*} \sup_{\mkern-10mu \frac{N}{\log^b N} \leqslant \xi \leqslant \frac{N}{2}} \biggl\lvert \frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^{M} \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\biggr\rvert \cdot \frac{1}{N}\sum_{r = 0}^{N - 1} \bigl(\Lambda(r)\bigr)^2 &= {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^{A + 1} N} \biggr) {\rm O}(\log N)\\ &= {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^A N} \biggr), \end{align*} as required.
nodes.statement_short: Multiply the bounds to get $O(\log^{-A}N)$.

nodes.name: Combine with Sigma_1
nodes.statement: Combining the above with \cref{prop:estimate-sigma1}, we have \begin{equation*} \sum_{\xi = 1}^{\frac{N}{2}} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2 \Biggl(\frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^M \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\Biggr) = {\rm O} \biggl(\frac{1}{\log^A N}\biggr), \end{equation*} and thus, by symmetry, \begin{equation*} \sum_{\xi = 1}^{N-1} \biggl\lvert \frac{\hat{\Lambda}(\xi)}{N} \biggr\rvert^2 \Biggl(\frac{1}{M} \sum_{m = 1}^M \mathrm{e}\biggl(\! -\frac{\xi \floor{m^c}}{N} \biggr)\Biggr) = {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^A N}\biggr). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: With Proposition 3.2 and symmetry, the full nontrivial sum is $O(\log^{-A}N)$.

nodes.name: Case 1 < c < 2
nodes.statement: As mentioned in the introduction, the case of \(1 < c < 2\) remains open.

nodes.name: Fractional polynomial version
nodes.statement: Let $f(x) = a_1 x^{c_1} + a_2 x^{c_2} + \ldots + a_k x^{c_k}$, $A > 1$ be given, $c_1 > 0$ a non-integer, $a_1 \neq 0$, and $c_1 > c_2 > \ldots > c_k$. Then there exists $B = B(f,A)$ such that \[ \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{m \leqslant M} \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{n \leqslant N} \Lambda(n) \Lambda\bigl(n + \floor{f(x)}\bigr) = 1 + {\rm O}\biggl(\frac{1}{\log^A N} \biggr), \] where $M = \frac{N^{1/c_1}}{\log^{B} N}$.
assumptions: Let $f(x) = a_1 x^{c_1} + a_2 x^{c_2} + \ldots + a_k x^{c_k}$, $A > 1$ be given, $c_1 > 0$ a non-integer, $a_1 \neq 0$, and $c_1 > c_2 > \ldots > c_k$.
nodes.statement_short: The main asymptotic should hold with $\lfloor m^c\rfloor$ replaced by $\lfloor f\rfloor$ for any fractional polynomial $f$.
